docs.title: 1.4 Sample throughput and output reduction
docs.text:
For two receivers delivering four bytes per complex sample:

\[ R_{IQ}=2\times10^7\times4=80{,}000{,}000\ \mathrm{B/s}=80\ \mathrm{MB/s}. \]

This is sample payload; it excludes transport overhead and memory-copy traffic. Each ring has 16 MiB of payload plus a 384-byte control block: 16,777,600 bytes per mapping, or 33,555,200 bytes for two rings. Capacity corresponds to 419.4304 ms per channel; usable scheduling headroom depends on current occupancy.

At a nominal five output frames/s:

Output configuration Spectrum payload rate Reduction relative to raw I/Q One float32 spectrum, 2048 bins 40,960 B/s 99.9488% Five float32 spectra 204,800 B/s 99.744% Five spectra including SOL2 headers 215,200 B/s 99.731%

The actual sample cadence is 199.9872 ms, slightly faster than five frames/s. The table uses the nominal cadence for readability and excludes UDP/IP/link overhead. These are reductions through integration and spectral processing, not lossless compression ratios. Storage retains four linear components rather than the five display products.

docs.title: 2.1 Process ownership
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    P["Parent: supervisor and DSP consumer"]
    P -->|"fork"| C1["Child 1: SDRplay acquisition"]
    P -->|"fork"| C2["Child 2: SDRplay acquisition"]
    C1 -->|"I/Q writes"| R1["CH1 POSIX SHM ring"]
    C2 -->|"I/Q writes"| R2["CH2 POSIX SHM ring"]
    R1 -->|"reads"| P
    R2 -->|"reads"| P
    P --> U["UDP outputs"]
    P --> S["Optional storage"]

Each child receives a serial number and SHM name. Each opens its own SDRplay API connection, finds that serial, selects tuner A, retrieves device parameters, initializes callbacks, and marks its ring ready. The parent attaches using the ring constructor's consumer argument false; children use producer argument true.

The implementation isolates receiver selection and callbacks in separate processes. This is the program's device-ownership model; no vendor-wide single-device restriction is asserted here. The vendor SDK's process and fork requirements remain external interface constraints, rather than properties demonstrated by this application.

docs.title: 2.2 Discovery before fork
docs.text:
The parent opens the API, enumerates devices, copies serial numbers, and closes the API before either fork. With no manual serial selection, exactly two discovered devices are required; serials are sorted before assignment. More than two requires explicit selection. Manual serial options must appear together and must differ.

Design rationale. Closing the discovery connection keeps receiver acquisition sessions local to their owning child processes. API discovery is complete before process creation; each child subsequently establishes its own API session. This sequence does not replace the vendor SDK’s fork-safety contract.

    ChildProcessGuard children;
    children.pid1 = ::fork();
    if (children.pid1 < 0) {
        std::cerr << "[LỖI HỆ THỐNG] Lỗi fork() tiến trình con Kênh 1: " << std::strerror(errno) << "\n";
        return 1;
    }
    if (children.pid1 == 0) {
        instance_lock.close_in_child();
        run_sdr_producer_process(1, ser_ch1, SolarConfig::SHM::CH1_NAME);
    }

Source: src/main.cpp, lines 861–870; analogous CH2 branch at lines 872–882.

docs.title: 2.3 Single-instance exclusion
docs.text:
SingleInstanceLock::acquire() uses an exclusive, nonblocking file lock before the parent removes old SHM names. The core excerpt below is verbatim from the uploaded source; surrounding error-handling lines are omitted.

        fd_ = ::open(lock_path_.c_str(), O_CREAT | O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC, 0666);
        if (fd_ < 0) {
            err_msg = "Không thể mở lock file " + lock_path_ + ": " + std::strerror(errno);
            return false;
        }
        if (::flock(fd_, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) != 0) {
            const int e = errno;
            ::close(fd_);
            fd_ = -1;
            err_msg = "Đã có một phiên solar_correlator hoặc bài test phần cứng khác đang giữ khóa (" +
                      lock_path_ + ": " + std::strerror(e) + "). Từ chối khởi chạy để bảo vệ SHM!";
            return false;
        }

Source: src/main.cpp, lines 326–338.

The lock path is /tmp/solar_correlator.lock. Acquisition failure aborts startup. A successful acquisition writes the owner PID. Child branches close their inherited lock descriptor using close_in_child(). The parent's release path unlocks and closes but deliberately leaves the inode in place; deleting and recreating the path could permit independent locks on different inodes.

The lock coordinates programs that honor the same locking convention. It is not an access-control boundary against unrelated processes that ignore the lock. The parent retains its lock object until after the later hardware guards are destroyed.

docs.title: 2.4 Lock-free SPSC ring buffers
docs.text:
ring_buffer.hpp implements one producer and one consumer per ring. ComplexSample contains two int16_t fields and is statically constrained to four bytes. A 384-byte, cache-line-aligned control block places head, tail, overflow count, readiness and stream gate on separate 64-byte boundaries. Compile-time assertions require atomic<uint32_t> and atomic<bool> to be always lock-free.

The producer owns head; the consumer owns tail. Producer publication is a release store to head after writing samples. The consumer acquires head before copying samples and release-stores tail after consumption. The producer acquires tail before reusing capacity. Own-index reads use relaxed ordering. Unsigned head-minus-tail arithmetic represents occupancy; indexing uses (position & (capacity-1)). Capacity must be a power of two no larger than 2^31, and an observed occupancy above capacity is an invariant violation.

A write is all-or-nothing: if an incoming callback block exceeds free capacity, write() increments overflow_cnt once and returns zero. Existing samples are not overwritten. The counter measures rejected write events, not the number of lost samples. main() treats that short write as a producer fault and stops acquisition.

read() and skip() advance by at most available occupancy; peek_from_tail() requires the complete requested snapshot and does not advance tail. flush() copies a committed head snapshot into tail. It discards queued data and does not establish a hardware start epoch.

Producer construction uses shm_open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_RDWR, 0600), sizes the object, and maps it with MAP_SHARED. Placement initialization constructs atomic objects and touches the payload. Attachment validates mapping size, magic, ABI version, capacity and mask. Creation and attachment use flock() with a five-second internal deadline; the lock-free claim applies to sample transfer, not bootstrap. The parent's nominal ten-second attachment loop contains these constructor calls and is not an exact upper bound on total attachment latency.

On Linux the objects are normally visible through /dev/shm. They are shared virtual-memory mappings, not a distinct class of “virtual RAM.” The implementation neither locks pages into memory nor establishes hard real-time scheduling. Its IPC contract explicitly targets Linux/GCC or Clang, a shared ABI and coherent normal memory; it is not a portable ISO C++ interprocess abstraction. Only the consumer may call read/peek/skip/flush/available-read, and teardown must not run concurrently with transfers.

docs.title: 2.5 Callback continuity monitoring
docs.text:
sdr_stream_callback() discards callbacks before the write gate is opened. Once enabled, it tracks the expected next firstSampleNum. Reset, absent callback parameters, sequence mismatch, short ring writes, or exceptions cause ready=false and g_child_running=false.

    auto& rb = *ctx->ring;
    if (!rb.is_stream_started()) return;
    auto fail = [&] { rb.set_ready(false); g_child_running.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed); };
    if (reset || !params) { fail(); return; }
    if (!numSamples) return;
    if (ctx->have_expected && params->firstSampleNum != ctx->expected_sample) { fail(); return; }
    ctx->expected_sample = static_cast<uint32_t>(params->firstSampleNum + numSamples);
    ctx->have_expected = true;
    try { if (rb.write(xi, xq, numSamples) != numSamples) fail(); }
    catch (...) { fail(); }

Source: src/main.cpp, lines 459–468.

The child's main loop sleeps in 25 ms intervals while callbacks perform acquisition. After the running flag clears, it calls Uninit, ReleaseDevice, and Close, then _exit(0). Consequently, a callback-detected fault does not necessarily produce a nonzero child exit code. The parent also monitors readiness and process termination. The event callback is empty, so no event-specific recovery or overload acknowledgement can be attributed to it.

docs.title: 3.1 Enum state versus displayed operating label
docs.text:
Seven enum values exist. ALIGNED and ALIGNED+CAL are display labels derived from RUNNING plus two flags; they are not additional enum states.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> STARTUP
    STARTUP --> ALIGNING: normal startup
    STARTUP --> UNALIGNED: skip alignment
    ALIGNING --> CALIBRATING: alignment returns; cal-phase enabled
    ALIGNING --> RUNNING: alignment returns; no phase calibration
    CALIBRATING --> RUNNING: calibration and observation preparation complete
    UNALIGNED --> RUNNING: observation preparation complete
    RUNNING --> RECOVERING: integration failure or detected overflow
    RECOVERING --> RUNNING: diagnostic recovery succeeds
    RECOVERING --> STOPPING: aligned mode or recovery failure
    STARTUP --> STOPPING: startup failure or cancellation
    ALIGNING --> STOPPING: failure or cancellation
    CALIBRATING --> STOPPING: failure or cancellation
    UNALIGNED --> STOPPING: failure or cancellation
    RUNNING --> STOPPING: signal or health failure
    STOPPING --> [*]

This diagram summarizes conceptual transitions. Some startup failures return before the common shutdown block and rely on the guards already constructed. Other health failures throw directly into the outer exception handler without entering RECOVERING. Source selection and priming are actions between the depicted stages, not separate enum states.

Enum Meaning in this file STARTUP Validation, discovery, producer launch and resource preparation ALIGNING Startup alignment acquisition UNALIGNED Diagnostic startup branch selected by skip-align CALIBRATING Optional one-cycle static phase measurement RUNNING Repeated integration/publication; display depends on alignment/calibration flags RECOVERING Handling a failed/discarded integration; restart is restricted to diagnostic mode STOPPING Termination requested or fatal condition reached

docs.title: 3.2 Hardware controls and safe defaults
docs.text:
set_gpio_level() runs pinctrl set <pin> op dh/dl through std::system() and reports command success. force_antenna_off() attempts both commands, driving the noise-control and RF-switch outputs LOW. Despite its name, the function commands noise OFF and antenna selection; it does not turn the antenna signal path off.

Normal alignment startup constructs HardwareGuard, explicitly reasserts RF switch HIGH and noise HIGH, and waits WARMUP_DELAY_MS. At observation selection, antenna corresponds to LOW/OFF and noise corresponds to HIGH/ON. SafeGpioOnExit issues the LOW commands again at destruction.

The configured outputs are GPIO 6 for the RF switch and GPIO 26 for the noise-source control. Both use active-HIGH calibration commands. HardwareGuard waits 200 ms during construction; main() then reasserts and checks both HIGH commands and waits another 200 ms. Thus normal startup contains two configured 200 ms warm-up waits before SHM attachment, in addition to the later 200 ms stream-gate warm-up. Antenna source selection waits 100 ms; noise selection waits the larger of warm-up and switch-settle delays, currently 200 ms.

The GPIO controls an external noise-source supply path. Software command completion is not physical readback of switch position or the nominal 15 V supply. HardwareGuard itself ignores system() status; the orchestrator supplements it with checked commands.

docs.title: 3.3 Resource preparation and stream gate
docs.text:
Startup order:

  1. Validate CLI; optionally perform configuration-only checking and exit.
  2. Install SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers and ignore SIGPIPE.
  3. Acquire the instance lock; load optional storage configuration and run storage startup checks.
  4. Construct the exit GPIO guard, command noise OFF/antenna, and unlink old SHM names.
  5. Discover receiver serials and close the discovery API connection.
  6. Fork both producers.
  7. For normal alignment, select calibration/noise and wait for hardware warm-up.
  8. Attach both SHM rings, with a nominal 10 s attachment deadline.
  9. Construct the correlator, optional aligner, vectors, UDP senders, and optional storage object.
  10. Wait for both ready flags, with a 15 s deadline measured from that wait's start.
  11. Open the two SHM write gates sequentially, wait 200 ms, then flush both rings.
  12. Perform alignment or select the diagnostic branch, optionally calibrate phase, select observation source, and prime the correlator.

The correlator creates its two single-precision FFTW forward plans with FFTW_MEASURE before ring writes are enabled. The alignment plans use FFTW_ESTIMATE. Two adjacent set_start_stream(true) calls are a software gate, not a simultaneous hardware sampling trigger.

docs.title: 3.4 Sample alignment
docs.text:
StartupAlignment::acquire() receives the two rings, snapshot size, retry limit, a callback that waits for sufficient samples, and a measurement callback invoking TimeAligner::measure_offset_from_buffers(). Snapshot waiting uses a 3000 ms timeout and health checks before and after. The maximum accepted integer residual is zero. If acquisition returns normally, the parent sets is_sample_aligned=true and checks health again.

TimeAligner peeks 131,072 samples from each tail without consuming them. It subtracts each channel's complex DC mean, computes two forward FFTs, multiplies X1 by conj(X2), and performs an inverse FFT. The inverse is divided by snapshot length before finding the maximum complex correlation magnitude. The peak index is converted to a signed circular lag; an exact half-snapshot peak is rejected as ambiguous.

The noise floor is the mean correlation magnitude outside a circular ±16-sample exclusion region around the peak. The estimator computes:

\[ \mathrm{PNR}=20\log_{10}\frac{r_{\mathrm{peak}}}{\overline{r}_{\mathrm{outside}}+10^{-6}}. \]

Estimator validity requires finite PNR ≥ 10 dB. Startup acceptance additionally requires PNR ≥ 20 dB and |lag| < snapshot_size/2. Positive lag advances CH1; negative lag advances CH2. Each attempt begins with independent flushes; a correction is followed by three fresh verification snapshots. Before each verification both tails advance by a complete snapshot, so candidate samples are not reused. Every verification must satisfy the confidence test and residual exactly zero in the main application. Failed verification restarts the attempt sequence; exhausted attempts throw.

The accepted condition is zero measured integer lag. It is not an assertion of zero fractional delay, absolute UTC synchronization or indefinite phase stability. This revision uses 131,072 samples, superseding the 65,536-sample value in the initial documentation brief.

docs.title: 3.5 Optional static phase calibration
docs.text:
--cal-phase requires alignment; CLI validation rejects its combination with --skip-align/--no-align. While the calibration noise path remains selected, the parent primes the correlator and executes one integration with initially zero phase correction. It rejects failed integration, newly observed overflow, nonfinite phase/coherence, or a result where no bin meets the coherence threshold.

                        if (coherence[k] >= kMinCalCoherence) {
                            // Output k is shifted; phi is indexed in natural FFT order.
                            phi_rad[(k + n_bins / 2) % n_bins] = phase_rad[k];
                            locked_phase_bins++;
                        } else {
                            phi_rad[(k + n_bins / 2) % n_bins] = 0.0f;
                        }
                    }

Source: src/main.cpp, lines 1156–1163.

Bins meeting coherence >= 0.10 contribute a measured phase. Other bins receive zero correction. The code translates shifted output indices to natural FFT order using (k+n_bins/2)%n_bins. is_phase_calibrated=true means at least one bin passed, not that every bin was calibrated. There is no repeated calibration loop in main().

The threshold applies to coherence amplitude gamma, not gamma squared. Phase calibration is a single startup measurement; it neither estimates channel gain nor establishes an absolute astronomical flux scale.

docs.title: 3.6 Observation source and paired discard
docs.text:
The fixed source for the session is antenna by default or noise when requested. In applicable branches the parent commands the source, waits the configured settling delay, and removes queued samples using a common boundary:

                const uint32_t boundary = std::max(rb1.available_read(), rb2.available_read());
                skip_pair(boundary);
                check_alignment_health();
                mark("observation_source.paired_boundary");

Source: src/main.cpp, lines 1212–1215.

The local skip_pair() helper waits until both rings contain the requested count, then advances both consumers by that count:

        auto skip_pair = [&](uint32_t count) {
            if (!wait_for_samples(count, 3000))
                throw std::runtime_error("Paired discard timeout/cancellation");
            if (rb1.skip(count) != count || rb2.skip(count) != count)
                throw std::runtime_error("Short paired discard");
        };

Source: src/main.cpp, lines 1073–1078.

Design rationale. Equal advancement preserves an already established relative sample-index relationship, provided no samples were lost and the ring operations satisfy their assumed contract. Independently flushing each ring after alignment would not provide the same paired-advance property.

The boundary is the maximum currently committed occupancy of either ring. It is explicitly not a bound on samples still in SDR/USB transport. Therefore this step cannot by itself certify that all switching transients are absent from future observations. A physical settling measurement would be needed for that claim. Overflow counts are checked around switching.

docs.title: 4.1 End-to-end dataflow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Antenna or calibration/noise path"] --> B["Two SDR receivers"]
    B --> C["USB transport"]
    C --> D["Per-device I/Q callbacks"]
    D --> E["Two SHM rings"]
    E --> F["Alignment and observation boundary"]
    F --> G["FXCorrelator: Welch integration"]
    G --> H["S11, S22, complex S12"]
    H --> I["dB, phase and coherence products"]
    I --> J["Independent UDP destinations"]
    H --> K["Optional storage aggregation"]

docs.title: 4.2 Welch state and integration execution
docs.text:
FXCorrelator allocates sample, FFT, accumulation and output arrays during construction. It builds a symmetric Hann window and computes energy from the actual stored float coefficients. Two single-precision FFTW plans use FFTW_FORWARD and FFTW_MEASURE.

prime_buffers() records the overflow baselines, reads exactly H=1024 paired samples, and marks the correlator primed. Each integration reads M further paired hops. Alternating sample-array halves preserve 50% overlap without shifting the entire time-domain window. The final half of an integration becomes the initial overlap of the next integration.

Each input component is scaled by 1/32768 and windowed before the FFT. Cross real/imaginary and both auto powers accumulate in double precision. On AArch64, unless SOLAR_DISABLE_NEON is defined, the X-engine processes two complex bins at a time with NEON: FP32 FFT values are widened to FP64 before multiplication. Other targets use a scalar loop. This explicit NEON path belongs to correlation/accumulation; the selected FFTW library's internal SIMD configuration is a separate build dependency.

A cycle-wide five-second deadline, cancellation checks and overflow-baseline checks run while waiting for hops and at completion. Exceptions invalidate priming. Fast-math compilation is rejected in correlator.cpp; CMake also supplies -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off for GNU/Clang.

The parent wrapper supports boolean- or void-returning APIs. In this revision process_integration_cycle() and prime_buffers() return void: a normal return plus the running flag is reported as success; processing faults throw.

                    bool cycle_ok = false;
                    std::string cycle_err_msg;
                    try {
                        cycle_ok = api_bridge::invoke_integration_cycle(
                            fx, rb1, rb2, phi_rad, s12_db, phase_rad, coherence);
                    } catch (const std::exception& ex) {
                        cycle_ok = false;
                        cycle_err_msg = ex.what();
                    }

Source: src/main.cpp, lines 1272–1280.

After an accepted cycle, main() converts auto powers to dB, creates a host timestamp, sends enabled products, and submits the four linear spectral components to storage.

docs.title: 4.3 Frequency axis
docs.text:
bin_to_freq_mhz() uses:

\[ f[k]=f_c+\left(k-\frac{N}{2}\right)\frac{f_s}{N},\qquad 0\le k<N. \]

For the configured N=2048, fs=10 MHz and fc=35 MHz:

\[ \Delta f=4.8828125\ \mathrm{kHz},\qquad f[k]=35\ \mathrm{MHz}+(k-1024)\times4.8828125\ \mathrm{kHz}. \]

Bin 0 is centered at 30 MHz; bin 1024 at 35 MHz; bin 2047 at 39.9951171875 MHz. The nominal upper band edge of 40 MHz is not the last bin center. This is bin spacing, not a measured passband or proof of usable edge sensitivity.

docs.title: 4.4 DSP convention and normalization
docs.text:
For channel i and Welch frame m, define the unnormalized transform of ADC-count samples:

\[ w[n]=\frac12\left(1-\cos\frac{2\pi n}{N-1}\right),\quad X_{i,m}[k]=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}w[n]x_i[n+mH]e^{-j2\pi kn/N}. \]

Let U be the sum of squares of the actual stored window coefficients. The reported spectra are:

\[ S_{ii}[k]=\frac{1}{MNU}\sum_{m=0}^{M-1}|X_{i,m}[k]|^2, \] \[ S_{12}[k]=\frac{e^{-j\phi_{\mathrm{cal}}[k]}}{MNU} \sum_{m=0}^{M-1}X_{1,m}[k]X_{2,m}^{*}[k]. \]

Internally the transform input is divided by 32768; the final normalization multiplies by 32768² to restore ADC-count² units. Static phase rotation is applied once after accumulation because it commutes with the frame sum. It changes complex phase but not magnitude or auto powers.

The cross-product convention is X1 × conj(X2). For a cross sum a+jb, rotation by exp(-j phi) gives real=a cos(phi)+b sin(phi) and imaginary=b cos(phi)-a sin(phi). Reversing channel order changes the phase sign.

The correlator reports amplitude coherence:

\[ \gamma[k]=\frac{|S_{12}[k]|}{\sqrt{S_{11}[k]}\sqrt{S_{22}[k]}}. \]

A zero denominator yields zero. Nonfinite output, negative powers or gamma greater than 1+10^-9 raise an exception; accepted gamma is clamped to [0,1]. Phase is atan2(Im,Re), with zero phase for zero magnitude. All output arrays are FFT-shifted using j=(k+N/2) mod N, while the phase-correction vector uses natural FFT order.

The normalization yields mean power per input FFT bin in ADC-count². It is not a power spectral density per Hz, dBm measurement or calibrated flux density. The nominal bin spacing is distinct from Hann equivalent noise bandwidth.

docs.title: 4.5 dB conversion and units
docs.text:
convert_linear_auto_power_to_db() replaces nonfinite or negative inputs with 10^-12, clamps other inputs to at least that floor, and computes:

\[ P_{\mathrm{dB}}=10\log_{10}\left(\max(P,10^{-12})\right) \]

for finite nonnegative P. The floor produces -120 dB. S12 uses the same 10 log10 rule on the complex cross-spectrum magnitude inside the correlator.

The display unit is dB re 1 ADC-count² per input FFT bin. Frequency grouping is described as a linear mean of input-bin powers, not a sum over grouped bandwidth; this distinction matters when interpreting output units.

docs.title: 4.6 Integration timing
docs.text:
For N=2048, H=1024, M=1953, and fs=10 MHz:

\[ T_{\mathrm{advance}}=\frac{MH}{f_s}=199.9872\ \mathrm{ms}, \] \[ T_{\mathrm{support}}=\frac{N+(M-1)H}{f_s}=200.0896\ \mathrm{ms}. \]

The first is the nominal sample advance per successive integration; the second is the sample support of M overlapping transforms. The configured sample geometry therefore gives a nominal 200 ms integration. CPU runtime, queue latency and output cadence must be measured. The archived host tests do not establish sustained Raspberry Pi throughput or hard real-time deadline compliance.

docs.title: 5.1 SOL2 v3 nonblocking telemetry
docs.text:
All enabled senders share a nonzero random session identifier created by getrandom(). Each accepted integration uses a common frame ID and timestamp across products. Defaults are defined by config.hpp and network_config.hpp:

Product Type ID Port Cross-spectrum magnitude, dB 1 9999 CH1 auto power, dB 2 9998 CH2 auto power, dB 3 9997 Phase, rad 4 9996 Amplitude coherence gamma 5 9995

The default IPv4 destination is 192.168.10.1. S12 cannot be disabled; port zero disables another product. Active ports must differ.

TelemetrySender creates SOCK_DGRAM | SOCK_NONBLOCK | SOCK_CLOEXEC sockets, requests a 256 KiB send buffer and uses MSG_DONTWAIT. Path-MTU discovery is set to IP_PMTUDISC_DO: an undersized path produces a send error rather than deliberate IP fragmentation. The send path performs no user-space allocation, retry or sleep.

Each spectrum is split into eight application-level chunks of 256 bins. A datagram contains a 52-byte header and 1024-byte payload, totaling 1076 bytes before UDP/IP headers. Integers and IEEE-754 binary32 payload words use big-endian order; no native C++ struct is serialized.

Byte offset Width Field 0 4 Magic 0x534F4C32, SOL2 4 2 Version, 3 for typed products 6 2 Header size, 52 8 8 Session ID 16 8 Frame ID 24 8 Host timestamp, microseconds 32 4 Integration frame count, 1953 36 4 Flags: bit 0 FFT-shifted; payload type shifted left by 8 40 2 Total bins, 2048 42 2 Chunk index, 0–7 44 2 Chunk count, 8 46 2 Bins per chunk, 256 48 4 Starting bin offset 52 1024 Float32 spectrum values

All payload values must be finite. On any failed datagram, the sender abandons the remainder of that product's frame and records the error and successfully queued chunk count. There is no retransmission or receiver acknowledgement. queued=true means that all eight datagrams were accepted by the local kernel; receiver delivery and complete reassembly remain separate concerns. The two-argument constructor retains legacy v2 behavior, but main() explicitly constructs typed v3 senders.

docs.title: 5.2 Timestamp semantics
docs.text:
current_utc_timestamp_us() reads system_clock and converts its epoch duration to microseconds. It is called after successful integration and auto-power conversion, before publication. This is a host processing-time timestamp, not an ADC sample's hardware timestamp. USB, SHM and processing latency are not measured by this timestamp; deployment clock discipline determines UTC accuracy.

Storage estimates sample support from a processing-time anchor at the start of a segment. It advances relative sample positions by M×H and preserves original backend timestamps. A nonconsecutive frame ID starts a new segment and anchor. These estimated UTC fields carry the UTC_ESTIMATED quality flag; they are not hardware timestamps.

docs.title: 5.3 Storage worker, aggregation and HDF5 lifecycle
docs.text:
CMake enables SOLAR_BUILD_STORAGE by default. The target links HDF5, SQLite3 and nlohmann_json, and defines SOLAR_STORAGE_ENABLED for the acquisition application. Runtime archiving additionally requires --config and storage.enabled=true. Configuration-only checking exits before SDR and GPIO initialization.

The pipeline is constructed with deferred startup. After optional phase calibration, start_observation() copies the current calibration, updates alignment metadata, and starts a worker thread. This occurs before observation-source switching; actual records are submitted only after source selection and final DSP priming.

                    if (storage) storage->try_submit(telemetry_frame_id,timestamp_us,
                        fx.auto_power1(),fx.auto_power2(),fx.cross_real(),fx.cross_imag());

Source: src/main.cpp, lines 1355–1356.

The DSP thread submits four double-precision arrays: S11, S22, Re(S12), Im(S12). A preallocated SPSC queue copies them into owned slots. Full queues and disabled/paused/error states reject records and increment a drop counter; main() does not inspect the returned enum. Storage failures can therefore degrade archival completeness while UDP/DSP continue. This differs from sample-continuity failures, which stop aligned acquisition.

The worker aggregates whole contiguous integrations to meet or exceed the requested save interval. The count is ceil(requested_interval/source_cadence). Frequency grouping computes linear means of contiguous bins. Temporal accumulation is weighted by valid FFT-frame counts, and all four components share a strict invalid-bin mask. Calibration changes and discontinuities terminate an aggregation window according to the configured emit/discard policy. Derived magnitude and phase must be computed from the averaged complex components rather than averaged dB or phase angles.

The checked-in config/solar_storage.json selects:

Setting Value Save interval 0.1999872 s; one source integration Saved frequency bins 2048 Queue capacity 150 records Append batch / HDF5 chunk rows 16 / 16 Rotation 15 minutes and observation-day boundaries Compression none; writer also supports gzip Periodic flush 10 s Shutdown drain timeout 15 s Per-file byte cap 200,000,000 bytes Daily budget 24,000,000,000 bytes

These settings preserve the input frequency grid and integration cadence; coarser archival reduction requires a different configuration. A file cap is enforced by the custom HDF5 VFD. It is not a promise of successful size-triggered rolling: cap/I/O failures enter quarantine/error handling. Free-space and budget checks may pause storage.

Files are created exclusively with a .tmp suffix. Normal closure appends remaining batch data, flushes/closes HDF5, publishes using no-replace renameat2, fsyncs the containing directory, and marks the artifact ready in the SQLite budget ledger. The custom VFD uses fsync for file flushes. Power-loss durability still depends on the filesystem and storage device.

HDF5 location Contents /metadata Configuration hash, session/source, revision, normalization, calibration and quality declarations /frequency_hz Float64 centers of saved frequency groups /calibration_phi_rad_unshifted Float32 phase-correction vector in natural FFT order /data/s11_linear, /data/s22_linear Extendable float32 auto spectra /data/s12_real, /data/s12_imag Extendable float32 phase-corrected cross spectra /data timing/identity fields Sample support, estimated UTC start/end/midpoint, backend timestamps, frame ranges and valid FFT count /data/quality_flags UTC estimate, invalid bin, partial window, discontinuity, calibration boundary and coherence-violation bits

Pipeline::stop() requests termination and joins its worker. The worker drains within the configured deadline, discards remaining queued records after that deadline, and handles its last partial aggregation according to policy. The drain timeout bounds queue-drain logic, not every possible blocking filesystem operation.

docs.title: 5.4 Automatic maintenance
docs.text:
AutoMaintenance launches scripts/storage_auto.py using posix_spawnp in a separate process group. The parent checks its process status every observation iteration; an unexpected exit throws and stops the observation. Shutdown sends SIGTERM to the group, waits up to five seconds, and uses SIGKILL as necessary.

The checked-in configuration enables quicklook generation, rclone-based remote synchronization and retention. These are delegated maintenance services, not work performed in the DSP integration loop. Configuration includes remote verification and cleanup policies; credentials, remote availability and successful execution are deployment requirements. The acquisition state machine and storage worker state machine remain distinct.

docs.title: 6.1 Health checks at multiple boundaries
docs.text:
The parent monitors child termination using waitpid(..., WNOHANG), ring readiness, and overflow counters. Alignment-mode health checks compare overflow counters against baselines initialized to zero; those baselines are not advanced in this file. Overflow from the stream-gate period is therefore treated as fatal even outside an integration boundary.

        auto check_alignment_health = [&]() {
            std::string err;
            if (!children.check_children_alive(err) || !rb1.is_ready() || !rb2.is_ready()) {
                mark("health.producer_failure");
                throw std::runtime_error("[ALIGNMENT_LOST] Producer stopped/reset: " + err);
            }
            if (!cli.skip_align &&
                (rb1.get_overflow_count() != aligned_drops1 ||
                 rb2.get_overflow_count() != aligned_drops2)) {
                mark("health.overflow");
                throw std::runtime_error("[ALIGNMENT_LOST] Sample drop since stream gate");
            }
        };

Source: src/main.cpp, lines 1060–1072.

The code also captures counts immediately before and after integration. A false cycle result, caught integration exception, or changed counter discards that cycle and enters the explicit recovery branch. A later health check occurs before output publication. Startup, source selection and calibration have additional checks.

These checks observe discrete boundaries. They do not form a transaction with callback execution or network transmission; a producer fault can occur after a health snapshot. Overflow counting uses a wrapping uint32_t rejected-write counter; callbacks stop on the first rejected write.

docs.title: 6.2 Why aligned acquisition stops on loss
docs.text:
A discontinuity can change the relationship between sample positions in the two channels. Static phase correction was obtained for a particular acquisition relationship. Resuming after arbitrary independent flushes would not demonstrate that this relationship still holds. The software therefore treats observed continuity loss as invalidating the existing observation contract instead of silently declaring alignment retained.

Failure handling:

Condition Visible response Child terminated or readiness false Health exception or supervisor stop; no automatic producer restart Overflow seen by normal-mode health check Exception and shutdown, potentially bypassing RECOVERING Failed cycle or overflow detected inside cycle boundary, phase calibrated Discard integration and stop Same cycle failure with skip-align enabled Independent flushes, re-prime and resume if permitted Same cycle failure in aligned, noncalibrated mode Stop More than five diagnostic recovery attempts Stop Failed diagnostic re-prime Stop

The diagnostic recovery counter is cumulative for the session; it is not reset after a successful cycle. The frame ID is incremented for a discarded integration so subsequent output can contain a visible gap. This does not identify packet losses that occur elsewhere.

docs.title: 6.3 Graceful shutdown and scope lifetimes
docs.text:
Common shutdown path:

  1. Exit the processing scope. Locally constructed DSP, sender, ring-reader and optional storage objects are destroyed as that scope ends.
  2. Set state to STOPPING and clear the parent running flag.
  3. Request HardwareGuard::turn_off() if present.
  4. Explicitly command noise OFF and antenna selection, including noise observations that skipped alignment.
  5. Send SIGTERM to remaining children and poll waitpid for up to 3000 ms.
  6. SIGKILL any remaining child and perform a blocking waitpid reap.
  7. Stop automatic maintenance when compiled in.
  8. Unlink both SHM names.
  9. On function exit, later-scope guards are destroyed before the instance lock is released. The GPIO exit guard repeats the safe-level commands.

This order matters: the storage pointer is inside the try scope, whereas maintenance and the hardware guard are outside it. The pipeline destructor calls stop() and joins the storage worker before the explicit post-scope acquisition teardown. Maintenance is stopped later by its own process-group shutdown routine. Some early returns follow different subsets of the sequence.

SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers set flags; they do not directly run teardown. The signal handlers use atomic boolean stores; the ring header statically requires atomic<bool> to be always lock-free for supported builds. The intended graceful path cannot cover power loss, SIGKILL of the parent, or failed physical actuators. Process reaping and GPIO command attempts are software actions, not physical-state certification.

docs.title: 7. Command-line reference
docs.text:
The following defaults are compiled from the baseline configuration.

Option Default Validation and behavior --dest-ip <ip> 192.168.10.1 IPv4 literal validated by inet_pton --port-s12 <port> 9999 1–65535; cannot disable --port-s11 <port> 9998 0–65535; 0 disables --port-s22 <port> 9997 0–65535; 0 disables --port-phase <port> 9996 0–65535; 0 disables --port-coherence <port> 9995 0–65535; 0 disables --skip-align, --no-align false Diagnostic branch; incompatible with cal-phase --input-source <antenna\|noise> antenna Fixed observation source selected after startup conditioning --cal-phase false One startup phase-calibration cycle after alignment --max-align-retries <n> 8 Integer 1–1000 --serial-ch1 <serial> automatic Must be supplied with serial-ch2; serials must differ --serial-ch2 <serial> automatic Must match a discovered device --config <path> absent Requires storage-enabled build; parser message refers to SOLAR_BUILD_STORAGE=ON --check-config false Requires config; validates/prints estimate and exits before SDR/GPIO startup -h, --help false Prints usage and exits

Enabled output ports must be pairwise distinct. Unknown options are rejected. Legacy --port-aux and --aux-mode are explicitly rejected with migration guidance. Help returns early during parsing, so it is not equivalent to validating all other supplied arguments.

docs.title: 7.1 Operation examples
docs.text:
The executable, serials, IP and configuration paths below are placeholders. Replace them with verified deployment values. These are invocation examples, not records of successful hardware runs.

# Aligned antenna observation; no static phase calibration requested.
/path/to/solar_correlator --input-source antenna

# Aligned antenna observation with one startup static phase calibration.
/path/to/solar_correlator --cal-phase --input-source antenna

# CW or dummy-load diagnostic acquisition; sample alignment is skipped.
/path/to/solar_correlator --skip-align --input-source antenna

# Noise observation following normal sample alignment.
/path/to/solar_correlator --input-source noise

# Noise observation following sample alignment and phase calibration.
/path/to/solar_correlator --cal-phase --input-source noise

# Explicit channel mapping and receiver destination.
/path/to/solar_correlator --serial-ch1 CH1_SERIAL --serial-ch2 CH2_SERIAL \
  --dest-ip 192.0.2.10 --port-s12 9999 --port-s11 9998 --port-s22 9997 \
  --port-phase 9996 --port-coherence 9995

# Storage-enabled observation using an existing configuration file.
/path/to/solar_correlator --config /path/to/observation.json --cal-phase

# Configuration-only validation and estimate; no receiver initialization.
/path/to/solar_correlator --config /path/to/observation.json --check-config

A dummy load or CW input is an external setup; selecting skip-align does not connect such a source. Selecting noise does not itself enable phase calibration. These distinctions should remain explicit in deployment procedures.

docs.title: 8. Implementation references and validation boundary
docs.text:
The implementation baseline is pinned at the beginning of this document. The source map below is the entry point for maintenance and review; source comments and older narrative documents do not override executable code or active configuration.

Concern Primary source Lifecycle, CLI, process supervision src/main.cpp RF, GPIO, SHM and alignment constants src/config.hpp FFT, sample rate and cadence src/dsp_config.hpp Destination address and protocol magic src/network_config.hpp Shared-memory ABI and SPSC operations src/ring_buffer.hpp Lag estimator and startup acceptance src/time_alignment.cpp, src/startup_alignment.hpp Hardware guard src/hardware_control.hpp Welch, normalization and NEON X-engine src/correlator.cpp SOL2 serializer and nonblocking sockets src/telemetry_sender.hpp Storage queue and aggregation src/storage/storage_queue.hpp, src/storage/storage_aggregator.cpp HDF5 pipeline and file limits src/storage/storage_pipeline.cpp, hdf5_writer.cpp, bounded_hdf5_vfd.cpp Maintenance process and configuration src/storage/storage_config.cpp, config/solar_storage.json Dependencies and compile flags CMakeLists.txt

docs.title: 8.1 Existing test evidence
docs.text:
The repository contains archived test results under docs/audit_v2/evidence. ctest.log records passes for telemetry-sender, storage-core and startup-alignment contracts. dsp.log records tone/phase tests, comparison against long-double DFT results, Parseval checks, cross-cycle overlap continuity, invalid-input and discontinuity cases. callback.log records callback sequence-wrap, gap, reset and full-ring cases. deferred.log records a queue-to-aggregation-to-HDF5/SQLite/quicklook smoke test.

These are checked-in historical results, not tests rerun for this documentation update. The DSP evidence explicitly limits itself to the host architecture and does not certify ARM execution time. It must not be presented as a new Raspberry Pi throughput or RF performance measurement.

docs.title: 8.2 Instrument-level limits
docs.text:
The implemented calibration contract consists of startup integer-sample alignment and optional static phase correction. A zero integer residual is not a fractional-delay measurement or hardware UTC anchor. Phase-calibrated status does not imply every frequency bin passed the calibration threshold. Fixed gain settings are not gain calibration, and ADC-count spectra are not calibrated solar flux measurements.

Absolute timing, analog passband flatness, receiver reference-lock state, long-term phase/gain stability and physical switching transients require instrument measurements. The software gates, sample counters, timestamp estimates and output metadata expose the corresponding software contracts without substituting for those measurements.

docs.title: Solar Radio Interferometer: Firmware & DSP Architecture Specification
docs.text: Document Path: docs/02-firmware-dsp/architecture.md Reference Repository: https://github.com/tuchau1404/solar_correlator Surveyed Source Code: src/main.cpp (Snapshot inspection; build metadata macros SOLAR_BASELINE_REVISION and SOLAR_PATCH_STATE referenced) Verification Scope & Limitations: Evaluated directly against src/main.cpp. The exact Git commit SHA is marked as Unverified from provided source due to the absence of the .git metadata directory in the examined workspace. All behaviors documented herein reflect direct code analysis, configuration bindings, and explicitly stated mathematical and engineering inferences.

docs.title: Section 1 — Overview & Scope
docs.text:
The src/main.cpp module serves as the Master Supervisor & Consumer Pipeline for the dual-element Solar Radio Correlator operating in the \(30.0 - 40.0\text{ MHz}\) frequency band. The program orchestrates the multi-process lifecycle of two SDRplay RSPdx software-defined radio receivers, coordinates hardware RF switching and noise calibration via Raspberry Pi 5 GPIO pins, enforces integer-sample time alignment, executes a pipelined Welch FX cross-correlator, and streams multi-product SOL2 v3 UDP telemetry alongside optional downsampled storage aggregation.

                      +---------------------------------------+
                      |          src/main.cpp (Parent)        |
                      |   Master Supervisor & Data Consumer   |
                      +---------------------------------------+
                        |                 |                 |
       Fork & Supervise |                 | Read I/Q        | Control GPIO
                        v                 v                 v
            +--------------------+   +----------+   +-------------------+

docs.title: Data Rate Reduction Analysis
docs.text:
The Welch cross-correlator performs lossy dimensionality reduction and temporal spectral integration. It reduces time-domain complex voltage series into integrated power and phase spectra; it is explicitly not lossless compression.

Derivation Assumptions: - Sampling rate: \(f_s = 10.0\text{ MSPS}\). - One full integration advances the stream by \(M \times H\) samples: $\(M \times H = 1953 \times 1024 = 1,999,872\text{ samples}\)$ - Frame period (cadence): $\(T_{\text{advance}} = \frac{1,999,872}{10,000,000\text{ samples/s}} = 0.1999872\text{ s} \approx 0.2\text{ s}\)$ - Output frame generation rate: $\(R_{\text{frame}} = \frac{1}{0.1999872\text{ s}} \approx 5.00032\text{ frames/s}\)$ - Each spectrum consists of \(N = 2048\) bins in 32-bit single-precision floating point format (\(4\text{ bytes/bin}\)), yielding \(2048 \times 4 = 8192\text{ bytes/vector}\).

  1. Single UDP Product (e.g., \(S_{12}\) Cross-Power only):
  2. Payload bandwidth: $\(\text{Rate}_{S12} = 8192\text{ bytes} \times 5.00032\text{ frames/s} \approx 40,962.6\text{ B/s} \approx 40.96\text{ kB/s} \approx 0.041\text{ MB/s}\)$

  3. Data reduction ratio relative to \(80.0\text{ MB/s}\) raw stream: $\(\text{Reduction Ratio} = \frac{80,000,000\text{ B/s}}{40,962.6\text{ B/s}} \approx 1953.0\times \quad (99.9488\%\text{ reduction})\)$

  4. All Five UDP Telemetry Products Enabled (\(S_{12}, S_{11}, S_{22}, \text{Phase}, \text{Coherence}\)):

  5. Combined payload per frame: \(5 \times 8192\text{ bytes} = 40,960\text{ bytes/frame}\).
  6. Aggregate telemetry egress rate: $\(\text{Rate}_{\text{all}} = 40,960\text{ bytes} \times 5.00032\text{ frames/s} \approx 204,813\text{ B/s} \approx 204.81\text{ kB/s} \approx 0.205\text{ MB/s}\)$

  7. Data reduction ratio: $\(\text{Reduction Ratio} = \frac{80,000,000\text{ B/s}}{204,813\text{ B/s}} \approx 390.6\times \quad (99.744\%\text{ reduction})\)$

  8. Storage Pipeline Egress:

  9. Governed dynamically by the JSON configuration schema via --config (save_freq_bins, save_interval_sec).
  10. Confirmed Behavior: Bins are downsampled to save_freq_bins and averaged across save_interval_sec. Egress bandwidth is dependent entirely on user-defined aggregation parameters.

docs.title: Device Enumeration & Multi-Process Decoupling
docs.text:
1. Pre-fork Hardware Probing: The parent process opens the SDRplay API service, locks the device table via sdrplay_api_LockDeviceApi(), queries available RSPdx units using sdrplay_api_GetDevices(), verifies or maps serial numbers, and explicitly closes the API with sdrplay_api_Close() prior to executing fork(): 

    // Excerpt: src/main.cpp (main)
(void)sdrplay_api_UnlockDeviceApi();
// ... serial matching logic ...
(void)sdrplay_api_Close();

std::string ser_ch1;
std::string ser_ch2;
// ... channel serial assignment ...

ChildProcessGuard children;
children.pid1 = ::fork();
if (children.pid1 == 0) {
    instance_lock.close_in_child();
    run_sdr_producer_process(1, ser_ch1, SolarConfig::SHM::CH1_NAME);
}
    Design Rationale: The proprietary SDRplay API runtime daemon communicates with client applications via internal IPC domains/sockets. Closing the API handle before fork() ensures child processes do not inherit active file descriptors or corrupted socket state [Inference based on multi-process POSIX socket behavior].

  2. Independent Child Acquisition: Each child independently invokes sdrplay_api_Open(), locks the service, matches its designated serial string, calls sdrplay_api_SelectDevice(), configures RF parameters, and initializes the device stream via sdrplay_api_Init().

  3. State Flag Differentiation:

  4. Device Init Completed: sdrplay_api_Init() returns sdrplay_api_Success. The driver threads commence packet ingestion.
  5. Hardware Ready Flag (is_ready()): Set to true by the child producer process only after sdrplay_api_Init() succeeds. Signifies to the parent that hardware registers are initialized.
  6. Stream Write Gate (is_stream_started()): Initialized to false. The stream callback discards incoming USB samples until the parent process issues rb.set_start_stream(true).
  7. Sample Aligned Flag (is_sample_aligned): Internal parent supervisor boolean, set to true exclusively when coarse cross-correlation achieves zero residual sample offset (\(k_{\text{residual}} = 0\)).

docs.title: Stream Callback Verification & Sample Discontinuity Detection
docs.text:
The high-throughput callback sdr_stream_callback executes within the SDRplay driver thread context. It rigorously validates sample packet continuity:

// Excerpt: src/main.cpp (sdr_stream_callback)
void sdr_stream_callback(short* xi, short* xq,
                         sdrplay_api_StreamCbParamsT* params,
                         unsigned int numSamples, unsigned int reset, void* cbContext) {
    auto* ctx = static_cast<StreamContext*>(cbContext);
    if (!ctx || !ctx->ring || !g_child_running.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return;
    auto& rb = *ctx->ring;
    if (!rb.is_stream_started()) return;
    auto fail = [&] { rb.set_ready(false); g_child_running.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed); };
    if (reset || !params) { fail(); return; }
    if (!numSamples) return;
    if (ctx->have_expected && params->firstSampleNum != ctx->expected_sample) { fail(); return; }
    ctx->expected_sample = static_cast<uint32_t>(params->firstSampleNum + numSamples);
    ctx->have_expected = true;
    try { if (rb.write(xi, xq, numSamples) != numSamples) fail(); }
    catch (...) { fail(); }
}
  • Hardware Reset Detection: If reset != 0 (indicating USB packet loss, clock re-lock, or driver resynchronization), the callback invokes fail(), invalidates ready, and terminates the child.
  • Sample Continuity Verification (firstSampleNum): The driver-supplied params->firstSampleNum is validated against ctx->expected_sample. A mismatch of even a single sample triggers an immediate fail-closed abort.
  • Short Write / Buffer Overflow: If rb.write() fails to write all numSamples into the ring buffer, fail() is triggered immediately.
  • Event Callback (sdr_event_callback): 
    // Excerpt: src/main.cpp (sdr_event_callback)
void sdr_event_callback([[maybe_unused]] sdrplay_api_EventT eventId,
                        [[maybe_unused]] sdrplay_api_TunerSelectT tuner,
                        [[maybe_unused]] sdrplay_api_EventParamsT* params,
                        [[maybe_unused]] void* cbContext) {}
    Confirmed Behavior: Hardware events (such as ADC overload, gain changes, or PLL unlock notifications) are currently unhandled and discarded.

docs.title: Lock-Free SPSC Ring Buffer over POSIX Shared Memory
docs.text:
• Ownership & Mutex-Free Synchronization: Implements a single-producer single-consumer circular buffer. The child producer exclusively mutates the head index; the parent consumer exclusively mutates the tail index.
  • Memory Ordering on ARM64: On Raspberry Pi 5 (quad-core ARM Cortex-A76, ARMv8.2-A), atomic operations on 32-bit and 64-bit primitives are natively lock-free. Memory consistency is maintained via Acquire-Release semantics (LDAR/STLR instructions) [Inference based on standard C++17 SPSC semantics].
  • Buffer Layout & Lifecycle: Mapped into virtual memory under POSIX shared memory identifiers /solar_correlator_ch1 and /solar_correlator_ch2. The parent guarantees isolation by unlinking both SHM names via SharedMemoryRingBuffer::unlink_shm() during initialization and upon shutdown.

docs.title: Single-Instance Process Mutex (SingleInstanceLock)
docs.text:
To prevent multiple instances from concurrently accessing SDRplay hardware or corrupting SHM nodes, SingleInstanceLock encapsulates an advisory file lock over /tmp/solar_correlator.lock:

// Excerpt: src/main.cpp (SingleInstanceLock::acquire)
bool acquire(std::string& err_msg) {
    fd_ = ::open(lock_path_.c_str(), O_CREAT | O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC, 0666);
    if (fd_ < 0) { /* handle error */ return false; }
    if (::flock(fd_, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) != 0) {
        const int e = errno;
        ::close(fd_);
        fd_ = -1;
        err_msg = "Another solar_correlator session is holding the lock (" +
                  lock_path_ + ": " + std::strerror(e) + "). Aborting to protect SHM!";
        return false;
    }
    acquired_ = true;
    const std::string pid_str = std::to_string(::getpid()) + "\n";
    if (::ftruncate(fd_, 0) != 0 ||
        ::write(fd_, pid_str.data(), pid_str.size()) != static_cast<ssize_t>(pid_str.size())) {
        err_msg = "Unable to record lock owner PID";
        release();
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}
  • Mechanism: Employs non-blocking exclusive locking (flock(fd, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)). Records the owner PID into the file upon acquisition.
  • Child Descriptor Cleanup: Child processes execute instance_lock.close_in_child() immediately after fork(), closing inherited file descriptors without releasing the parent's lock.
  • Preservation of Inode: The file lock is unlocked via flock(fd_, LOCK_UN) upon destructor invocation. The lock file is intentionally not unlinked. Unlinking the inode while open would permit a competing process to create a distinct inode at the same pathname, breaking mutual exclusion.

docs.title: State Machine Transition Topology
docs.text:
The system transitions across seven discrete states defined by enum class SystemState:

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> STARTUP : System Boot & Parameter Validation
    STARTUP --> STOPPING : Hardware Error / SHM Timeout / SIGINT
    STARTUP --> UNALIGNED : Flag --skip-align / --no-align enabled
    STARTUP --> ALIGNING : Default startup path

    ALIGNING --> STOPPING : Continuity Loss / Retries Exhausted / Producer Fault
    ALIGNING --> CALIBRATING : Alignment Locked (k=0) & --cal-phase enabled
    ALIGNING --> RUNNING : Alignment Locked (k=0) & --cal-phase disabled

    UNALIGNED --> RUNNING : Observation Source Set & Prime Buffers

    CALIBRATING --> STOPPING : Coherence Floor Failed / Buffer Overflow
    CALIBRATING --> RUNNING : Phase Vector phi_rad Locked

    RUNNING --> STOPPING : Producer Crash / Signal Received (SIGINT/SIGTERM)
    RUNNING --> RECOVERING : Cycle Interrupted / Buffer Overflow Detected

    RECOVERING --> STOPPING : is_phase_calibrated == true (Fail-Closed)
    RECOVERING --> STOPPING : is_sample_aligned == true (Fail-Closed)
    RECOVERING --> STOPPING : Diagnostic UNALIGNED retries > 5
    RECOVERING --> RUNNING : Diagnostic Recovery OK (retries <= 5)

    STOPPING --> [*] : Safe GPIO Release, Child Reaping & SHM Unlink

docs.title: Enumerations, Display Strings, and Operational Flags
docs.text:
The control logic differentiates internal state enumerations, UI reporting strings, and verification flags:

Internal Enum (SystemState) Flag is_sample_aligned Flag is_phase_calibrated Display String (state_to_string) Operational Meaning STARTUP false false "STARTUP" Initializing memory, probing SDRs, preallocating DSP pipelines. ALIGNING false false "ALIGNING" Cross-correlating reference noise snapshots to eliminate delay \(k\). UNALIGNED false false "UNALIGNED" Delay alignment bypassed via --skip-align (diagnostic mode). CALIBRATING true false "CALIBRATING" Integrating noise periodograms to compute instrumental phase vector \(\phi_{\text{cal}}[k]\). RUNNING false false "UNALIGNED" Correlating live data without sample alignment verification. RUNNING true false "ALIGNED" Production correlation with integer alignment locked (\(k = 0\)). RUNNING true true "ALIGNED+CAL" Production correlation with integer delay locked and phase vector applied. RECOVERING (preserved) (preserved) "RECOVERING" Interrupted integration or ring buffer overflow detected. STOPPING (any) (any) "STOPPING" Graceful termination, child teardown, and resource unlinking.

docs.title: Hardware Control & Protective Guards
docs.text:
• GPIO Allocations:
  • SolarConfig::Hardware::PIN_RF_SWITCH (GPIO 6): High-frequency RF switch directing receiver inputs between noise calibration and antenna feeds.
  • SolarConfig::Hardware::PIN_NOISE_SOURCE (GPIO 26): Power gate for the broadband reference noise diode.
  • Control Interface: Invokes the Raspberry Pi utility pinctrl set <pin> op <dh|dl> via std::system().
  • Logic Polarity: Logic HIGH (dh) engages the noise source and connects the RF switch to the splitter; Logic LOW (dl) turns off the noise source and connects to the antenna feeds.
  • Fail-Safe Scoping (HardwareGuard & SafeGpioOnExit): force_antenna_off() commands both pins to LOW. The RAII struct SafeGpioOnExit guarantees that regardless of exceptions or stack unwinding, force_antenna_off() is executed.
  • Physical Limitation: Issuing shell commands to pinctrl confirms only that the Linux kernel processed the pin state request; it does not provide closed-loop telemetry confirming actual relay contact closure or noise diode bias current.

docs.title: Startup Pipeline & DSP Preallocation
docs.text:
1. Pre-Stream DSP Allocation: The parent initializes FXCorrelator (triggering FFTW plan generation via FFTW_MEASURE), constructs TimeAligner, instantiates TelemetrySender, and allocates storage buffers prior to opening the SHM stream gate. Design Rationale: Prevents 80 MB/s incoming sample streams from overflowing the ring buffers while the CPU is executing intensive FFTW planning benchmarks.
  2. Warm-up & Flush Procedure: Once both child producers report rb1.is_ready() and rb2.is_ready(): 
    // Excerpt: src/main.cpp (main)
rb1.set_start_stream(true);
rb2.set_start_stream(true);
// 200 ms settling delay for DMA stabilization
std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(200));
rb1.flush();
rb2.flush();
    Flushing purges unaligned sample transients accumulated during driver startup.

docs.title: Time Alignment Procedure
docs.text: Executed within ALIGNING via StartupAlignment::acquire(): - Captures snapshots of \(65,536\) samples simultaneously from both channel buffers. - TimeAligner::measure_offset_from_buffers() computes time-domain cross-correlation to estimate sample lag \(k\). - Acceptance Criterion: options.max_residual_samples = 0. The system strictly requires exact integer-sample convergence: $\(k_{\text{residual}} = 0\)$ - Retry Bounds: Up to cli.max_align_retries attempts (default 8). Failure to lock within this limit triggers an immediate runtime exception. - Physical Meaning: Achieving \(k_{\text{residual}} = 0\) confirms that sample frame boundaries between channels are matched to within one sample period (\(\Delta t = 1/f_s = 100\text{ ns}\)). This does not imply zero fractional delay, nor does it guarantee absence of long-term local oscillator phase drift.

docs.title: Static Phase Calibration (--cal-phase)
docs.text:
When --cal-phase is supplied, the system enters CALIBRATING: 1. Maintains noise source and RF calibration switch in the active state. 2. Executes prime_buffers() to load the initial 50% overlap. 3. Runs exactly one full Welch integration cycle (\(1953\) frames) via invoke_integration_cycle() to produce phase spectrum \(\theta_{\text{meas}}[k]\) and coherence amplitude \(\gamma[k]\). 4. Confirms zero buffer overflows occurred during calibration (\(ov_{\text{after}} == ov_{\text{before}}\)). 5. Bin Masking & Coherence Validation: 

// Excerpt: src/main.cpp (main)
constexpr float kMinCalCoherence = 0.10f;
size_t locked_phase_bins = 0;
// ...
for (size_t k = 0; k < n_bins; ++k) {
    if (!std::isfinite(phase_rad[k]) || !std::isfinite(coherence[k])) {
        throw std::runtime_error("[FAIL-CLOSED] Non-finite phase/coherence during calibration!");
    }
    mean_coherence += static_cast<double>(coherence[k]);
    if (coherence[k] >= kMinCalCoherence) {
        phi_rad[(k + n_bins / 2) % n_bins] = phase_rad[k];
        locked_phase_bins++;
    } else {
        phi_rad[(k + n_bins / 2) % n_bins] = 0.0f;
    }
}
if (locked_phase_bins == 0) {
    throw std::runtime_error("[FAIL-CLOSED] Zero frequency bins met Coherence >= 0.10 threshold!");
}
- Threshold: \(\gamma[k] \ge 0.10\). - Failing bins are clamped to correction phase \(\phi_{\text{cal}} = 0.0\text{ rad}\). - FFT Shift Mapping: The output array phase_rad[k] is DC-centered; the correction vector phi_rad is indexed in natural FFT order. Index transformation (k + n_bins / 2) % n_bins correctly maps the frequencies. - Fail-Closed Abort: Any non-finite value (NaN/Inf) or total failure to obtain at least one bin meeting coherence terminates execution.

docs.title: Observation Source Transition & skip_pair() Watermark
docs.text:
Following alignment or calibration, the supervisor commands the hardware to switch to --input-source (default antenna): 1. Disables HardwareGuard and drives GPIOs to target states. 2. Sleeps for SWITCH_SETTLE_MS (or WARMUP_DELAY_MS) to allow RF transients to decay. 3. Paired Watermark Sample Discard (skip_pair()): 

// Excerpt: src/main.cpp (main)
const uint32_t boundary = std::max(rb1.available_read(), rb2.available_read());
skip_pair(boundary);
check_alignment_health();
Reads the maximum available sample backlog across both channels and advances both ring buffer read pointers by that exact count. Physical Boundary Limitation: This establishes an identical watermark across the shared memory ring buffers. It cannot flush in-flight samples already buffered in the SDRplay kernel/USB hardware pipelines at the moment of GPIO switching. 4. Re-executes prime_buffers() to seed the 50% overlap state prior to entering RUNNING.

docs.title: DSP Implementation Specifics
docs.text:
1. Overlap Seeding (prime_buffers()): To sustain continuous 50% Welch overlap (\(N = 2048, H = 1024\)), prime_buffers() ingests the initial \(N - H = 1024\) samples from each ring buffer into internal history buffers. Each subsequent frame reads \(H = 1024\) fresh samples, concatenating them with the historical segment.
  2. Window Function: Applies a symmetric Hann window of length \(N = 2048\): $\(w[n] = 0.5 - 0.5 \cos\left(\frac{2\pi n}{N - 1}\right), \quad n = 0, 1, \dots, N-1\)$ The exact accumulated window energy \(W_{\text{ss}} = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} w[n]^2\) is computed directly from floating-point coefficients and included in the normalization factor.
  3. Cross-Correlation & Phase Correction: For frame \(m\) (\(m = 0 \dots M-1\)) at bin \(k\), the cross-spectral product incorporates complex conjugation of Channel 2 and the calibration phase rotation vector: $\(C_{12,m}[k] = X_{1,m}[k] \cdot X_{2,m}^*[k] \cdot e^{-j \phi_{\text{cal}}[k]}\)$
  4. Integration & Energy Normalization: The accumulated cross-power spectrum is normalized by integration frame count \(M\), transform size \(N\), and window energy: $\(S_{12}[k] = \frac{1}{M \cdot N \cdot \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} w[n]^2} \sum_{m=0}^{M-1} C_{12,m}[k]\)$ Auto-power spectra \(S_{11}[k]\) and \(S_{22}[k]\) are computed analogously from \(|X_{1,m}[k]|^2\) and \(|X_{2,m}[k]|^2\).
  5. Coherence Formulation: Coherence is evaluated as amplitude coherence (gamma) \(\gamma[k]\), not magnitude-squared coherence (\(\gamma^2\)): $\(\gamma[k] = \frac{\left|S_{12}[k]\right|}{\sqrt{S_{11}[k] \cdot S_{22}[k]}}\)$ The resulting metric \(\gamma[k]\) is bounded strictly within \([0.0, 1.0]\).
  6. Decibel Conversion & Clamping Policy: Linear auto-power and cross-power spectra are mapped to decibels with a \(10^{-12}\) lower bound clamp: 
    // Excerpt: src/main.cpp (convert_linear_auto_power_to_db)
void convert_linear_auto_power_to_db(const std::vector<double>& linear_val,
                                     std::vector<float>& out_db) noexcept {
    const size_t n = std::min(linear_val.size(), out_db.size());
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {
        const double v = linear_val[k];
        const double clamped = (std::isfinite(v) && v >= 0.0) ? std::max(v, 1e-12) : 1e-12;
        out_db[k] = static_cast<float>(10.0 * std::log10(clamped));
    }
}
  7. Mathematical formula: $\(P_{\text{dB}}[k] = 10 \log_{10}\left(\max\left(P[k], 10^{-12}\right)\right)\)$
  8. Non-finite Value Policy: Any NaN, +Inf, -Inf, or negative values are clamped to \(10^{-12}\), corresponding to a fixed floor of \(-120.0\text{ dB}\).
  9. Physical Units: Spectral power units are uncalibrated \(\text{ADC-count}^2\) per FFT bin. They do not represent absolute milliwatts (\(\text{dBm}\)) or calibrated astronomical flux units (Jansky).

docs.title: Frequency Bin Mapping & Spectral Resolution
docs.text:
FFT shift is performed to center the local oscillator (zero intermediate frequency) at bin \(k = N/2 = 1024\). The physical center frequency for bin \(k \in [0, N-1]\) is given by: $\(f[k] = f_c + \left(k - \frac{N}{2}\right) \frac{f_s}{N}\)$

Substituting actual system parameters (\(f_c = 35.0\text{ MHz}\), \(f_s = 10.0\text{ MSPS}\), \(N = 2048\)): - Bin Width (Frequency Resolution): $\(\Delta f = \frac{f_s}{N} = \frac{10,000,000\text{ Hz}}{2048} = 4882.8125\text{ Hz} = 4.8828125\text{ kHz}\)$ - First Bin Center (\(k = 0\)): $\(f[0] = 35.0\text{ MHz} + (0 - 1024) \times 4.8828125\text{ kHz} = 30.0000000\text{ MHz}\)$ - Center / DC Bin (\(k = 1024\)): $\(f[1024] = 35.0\text{ MHz} + (1024 - 1024) \times 4.8828125\text{ kHz} = 35.0000000\text{ MHz}\)$ - Final Bin Center (\(k = 2047\)): $\(f[2047] = 35.0\text{ MHz} + (2047 - 1024) \times 4.8828125\text{ kHz} = 39.9951171875\text{ MHz}\)$

Nyquist Edge vs. Bin Center: The nominal double-sided Nyquist span extends from \(30.0000000\text{ MHz}\) to \(40.0000000\text{ MHz}\). The center of the highest bin (\(k=2047\)) resides at \(39.9951171875\text{ MHz}\), with its upper edge extending to: $\(39.9951171875\text{ MHz} + \frac{4.8828125\text{ kHz}}{2} = 39.99755859375\text{ MHz}\)$

docs.title: Welch Temporal Geometry
docs.text:
A clear distinction must be maintained between temporal stream advance, total data support window, and CPU wall-clock execution time:

  1. Advance Time (\(T_{\text{advance}}\)): $\(T_{\text{advance}} = \frac{M \cdot H}{f_s} = \frac{1953 \times 1024}{10,000,000} = 0.1999872\text{ s}\)$ The time separation between the leading edges of consecutive integration blocks.
  2. Support Time (\(T_{\text{support}}\)): $\(T_{\text{support}} = \frac{N + (M - 1) H}{f_s} = \frac{2048 + (1953 - 1) \times 1024}{10,000,000} = \frac{2,000,896}{10,000,000} = 0.2000896\text{ s}\)$ The complete physical duration of the time-domain signal contributing to an integrated frame (exceeding \(T_{\text{advance}}\) by exactly \(1024\text{ samples} \equiv 100\text{ \mu s}\) due to initial window overlap).
  3. CPU Execution Wall-Clock Time: The elapsed processing time spent by the Raspberry Pi 5 executing invoke_integration_cycle(). To sustain real-time operation without ring buffer overflow, the execution time must strictly satisfy: $\(T_{\text{CPU}} < T_{\text{advance}} \quad (\approx 200\text{ ms})\)$

docs.text:
The SOL2 v3 protocol distributes data products across up to five independent UDP destination ports:

docs.title: SOL2 v3 UDP Protocol Characteristics
docs.text:
• Packet Chunking & Fragmentation: A vector of \(2048\) floating-point bins (\(8192\text{ bytes}\)) exceeds the standard Ethernet MTU (\(1500\text{ bytes}\)). The TelemetrySender partitions each spectral payload into multiple chunk datagrams.
  • Header & Sequencing: Header fields encode session_id, frame_id, total chunk count, current chunk index, payload type discriminator (Payload::S12, S11, S22, Phase, Coherence), and microsecond timestamp timestamp_us.
  • Egress Accounting: 
    // Excerpt: src/main.cpp (api_bridge::accumulate_telemetry_result)
inline void accumulate_telemetry_result(const TelemetrySender::Result& res,
                                        PortTelemetryStats& st) noexcept {
    st.chunks_sent_total += res.datagrams;
    if (res.queued) ++st.frames_complete;
    else {
        ++st.send_errors;
        if (res.datagrams > 0) ++st.frames_partial;
    }
}
    The pipeline tracks completed frames (frames_complete), truncated transfers (frames_partial), and socket enqueue errors (send_errors).
  • Send vs. Delivery Semantics: res.queued == true denotes non-blocking submission to the local Linux network socket buffer. Because UDP is connectionless and unacknowledged, transmission from the host provides no guarantee of packet reception at the downstream client.
  • Timestamp Provenance: 
    // Excerpt: src/main.cpp (current_utc_timestamp_us)
uint64_t current_utc_timestamp_us() noexcept {
    const auto now = std::chrono::system_clock::now();
    return static_cast<uint64_t>(
        std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::microseconds>(now.time_since_epoch()).count());
}
    Confirmed Behavior: Telemetry timestamps are Host Wall-Clock Timestamps derived from the Linux kernel clock. They are not hardware-latched timestamps generated from GPS/PPS or RSPdx hardware sample counters. Latencies introduced by USB transport and kernel scheduling remain uncompensated.

docs.title: Archival Storage Pipeline
docs.text:
• Compilation & Activation Gates: Compiled conditionally via -DSOLAR_BUILD_STORAGE=ON (defining SOLAR_STORAGE_ENABLED). Activated at runtime by supplying --config <path_to_json>.
  • Offline Configuration Verification (--check-config): Parses the storage JSON specification, executes validation checks, prints configuration hashes and storage rate estimates, and exits cleanly without initializing hardware.
  • Data Ingestion: Receives un-decibelized linear auto-powers (auto_power1, auto_power2) and raw complex cross-power components (cross_real, cross_imag) via storage->try_submit().
  • Queueing & Backpressure: Employs non-blocking submission semantics (try_submit). If disk I/O saturates internal queue depth, frames are discarded to prevent backpressure from stalling real-time DSP execution.
  • Background Maintenance: A dedicated helper thread (solar::storage::AutoMaintenance) monitors filesystem capacity, enforces retention policies, and executes directory maintenance during live runs.
  • Unverified Features: Storage container formatting (e.g., raw binary, HDF5, or FITS) and automatic cloud/network replication are handled within external translation units not present in src/main.cpp.

docs.title: Health Invariants & Continuity Checks
docs.text:
The supervisor performs continuity and health audits across three distinct pipeline stages:

// Excerpt: src/main.cpp (check_alignment_health)
auto check_alignment_health = [&]() {
    std::string err;
    if (!children.check_children_alive(err) || !rb1.is_ready() || !rb2.is_ready()) {
        mark("health.producer_failure");
        throw std::runtime_error("[ALIGNMENT_LOST] Producer stopped/reset: " + err);
    }
    if (!cli.skip_align &&
        (rb1.get_overflow_count() != aligned_drops1 ||
         rb2.get_overflow_count() != aligned_drops2)) {
        mark("health.overflow");
        throw std::runtime_error("[ALIGNMENT_LOST] Sample drop since stream gate");
    }
};

The Fundamental Axiom of Independent Receiver Interferometry: When two independent SDR receivers lack a hardware genlock / shared sample-clock distribution line, any uncorrected sample loss immediately destroys relative phase and delay calibration. It is physically invalid to assume two independent channels retain integer alignment after any sample drop. Consequently, any detected buffer overflow or producer reset invalidates the calibration state.

docs.title: Fault Classification & Fail-Closed Recovery Flowchart
docs.text:
Fault detected in RUNNING loop (!cycle_ok || overflow_occurred)
                         |
                         v
            Increment telemetry_frame_id (Visible sequence gap)
            Transition SystemState -> RECOVERING
                         |
         +---------------+---------------+
         |                               |
         v                               v
[is_phase_calibrated == true]     [cli.skip_align == true]
   Phase vector invalidated          Diagnostic CW / Dummy Load Mode
         |                               |
         v                               +---> diag_recovery_count <= 5:
   FAIL-CLOSED                              Flush SHM -> prime_buffers()
   Immediate System Abort!                  Resume RUNNING.
   exit_code = 1                         |
                                         +---> diag_recovery_count > 5:
                                                    FAIL-CLOSED -> STOPPING
                                         |
                                         v
                         [is_sample_aligned == true (Default)]
                            Sample alignment lost (k != 0)
                                         |
                                         v
                                    FAIL-CLOSED
                                 Immediate System Abort!
                                 exit_code = 1
  • Frame Discontinuity Signaling (++telemetry_frame_id): When an integration cycle aborts due to overflow or arithmetic failure, telemetry_frame_id is incremented. This introduces a visible sequence gap in downstream UDP streams, ensuring archiving systems detect missing data.
  • Diagnostic Mode Recovery (--skip-align): Only when sample alignment is explicitly bypassed does the system permit transient recovery. Up to 5 consecutive recoveries (kMaxDiagRecoveries = 5) are permitted via rb.flush() and buffer re-priming.
  • Fail-Closed Policy for Scientific Observation: In standard scientific observation modes (ALIGNED or ALIGNED+CAL), any sample drop causes an immediate fail-closed termination (exit_code = 1). Corrupted data is never permitted to masquerade as valid astronomical observations.

docs.title: System Shutdown & Resource Teardown
docs.text:
Upon receiving termination signals (SIGINT, SIGTERM) or encountering fatal errors, teardown proceeds through deterministic RAII scopes:

// Excerpt: src/main.cpp (ChildProcessGuard::terminate_and_reap_all)
void terminate_and_reap_all() noexcept {
    if (pid1 > 0) (void)::kill(pid1, SIGTERM);
    if (pid2 > 0) (void)::kill(pid2, SIGTERM);

    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::milliseconds(3000);
    while ((pid1 > 0 || pid2 > 0) && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) {
        if (pid1 > 0 && ::waitpid(pid1, &st, WNOHANG) == pid1) pid1 = -1;
        if (pid2 > 0 && ::waitpid(pid2, &st, WNOHANG) == pid2) pid2 = -1;
        if (pid1 <= 0 && pid2 <= 0) break;
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(25));
    }
    // Escalate to SIGKILL after 3.0-second grace period
    if (pid1 > 0) { (void)::kill(pid1, SIGKILL); (void)::waitpid(pid1, &st, 0); pid1 = -1; }
    if (pid2 > 0) { (void)::kill(pid2, SIGKILL); (void)::waitpid(pid2, &st, 0); pid2 = -1; }
}
  1. Hardware Safe State Assertion: Invokes hw_guard->turn_off() and force_antenna_off(), driving GPIO 6 and GPIO 26 to LOW.
  2. Child Process Reaping: Issues SIGTERM to both child producers, allowing up to 3.0 seconds for orderly device de-initialization. If a child hangs, the supervisor escalates to SIGKILL and reaps the PID via waitpid().
  3. Storage Pipeline Termination: Calls auto_maintenance.stop() to synchronize outstanding file handles.
  4. POSIX Shared Memory Unlinking: Calls SharedMemoryRingBuffer::unlink_shm() for /solar_correlator_ch1 and /solar_correlator_ch2, removing files from /dev/shm.
  5. Process Lock Release: Destructs SingleInstanceLock, executing flock(fd, LOCK_UN) and closing the file descriptor.
