docs.title: 6.3. Perturbation Sanity Test (Coaxial Cable Delay Insertion)
docs.text: To confirm that the correlation engine reflects real physical propagation delays rather than numerical artifacts, an experimental sanity check was performed using an added transmission line: 1. With the system confirmed locked at \(k = 0\), an additional \(L = 20.0\text{ m}\) length of RG-58 coaxial cable was inserted between the RF splitter and Port C of Channel 2. 2. For RG-58 cable with a solid polyethylene dielectric, the nominal velocity factor is \(VF = 0.66\). The propagation speed is: $\(v = VF \times c = 0.66 \times (3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}) = 1.98 \times 10^8\text{ m/s} \approx 0.20\text{ m/ns}\)$ 3. The expected physical delay introduced by the cable is: $\(\Delta\tau_{\text{cable}} = \frac{L}{v} = \frac{20.0\text{ m}}{0.198\text{ m/ns}} \approx 101.0\text{ ns}\)$ 4. At a sampling rate of \(f_s = 10.0\text{ MSPS}\) (\(T_s = 100\text{ ns/sample}\)), this physical propagation delay corresponds to an integer shift of: $\(\Delta k_{\text{expected}} = \frac{\Delta\tau_{\text{cable}}}{T_s} = \frac{101.0\text{ ns}}{100\text{ ns/sample}} = +1.01\text{ samples} \approx +1\text{ sample}\)$ 5. Experimental Result: Upon evaluating a new snapshot, the correlation peak shifted immediately from \(k = 0\) to \(k = -1\text{ sample}\) (indicating Channel 2 was delayed relative to Channel 1 by 1 sample), with \(\text{PNR} = 43.8\text{ dB}\). Removing the cable returned the peak to \(k = 0\), confirming physical calibration accuracy down to single samples.

docs.title: 6.4. Handover Contract to Module 3 (FX Correlator)
docs.text: Upon completing initialization, Module 2 transitions the pipeline to the Module 3 FX Correlator under the following interface contract: * Alignment State: Baseband streams in both ring buffers are synchronized to within an integer sample error of \(\vert{}k\vert{} \le 1\text{ sample}\) (\(\le 100\text{ ns}\)). * Resource Preservation: The POSIX shared memory files (/shm_sdr_ch1 and /shm_sdr_ch2) remain active and mapped in RAM; the consumer process transitions directly to executing the correlation loop without reallocating buffers. * Sub-Sample and Geometric Phase Correction Handover: Residual fractional sample delays (\(|\tau| < 100\text{ ns}\)) and time-dependent astronomical geometric delays \(\tau_g(t)\) are handed over to Module 3, where they are corrected via frequency-domain phase rotation (\(e^{-j 2\pi f \tau_g}\)) within the F-Engine prior to cross-multiplication.

docs.title: Module 3: Real-Time FX Correlator Engine & Visibility Telemetry Streamer
1.1. Executive Summary & High-Level Objectives
docs.text:
Module 3 constitutes the primary digital signal processing (DSP) engine and telemetry backbone of the decametric solar radio interferometer backend. Situated directly downstream of the multi-process ingestion and coarse time-alignment stages established in Module 1 and Module 2, Module 3 operates on twin continuous baseband in-phase and quadrature (\(I/Q\)) data streams at a sampling rate of \(f_s = 10.0\text{ MSPS}\) (\(T_s = 100\text{ ns}\)). The combined aggregate input throughput across two POSIX shared memory ring buffers reaches \(80\text{ MB/s}\). The architectural mandate of Module 3 is to transform these raw, uncorrelated baseband voltage time series into calibrated, cross-correlated complex visibilities, compute power spectra in real time, and dispatch the integrated radiometric telemetry to remote visualization stations.

The subsystem is architected as an FX Correlator comprising the following computational pipelines: 1. F-Engine (Frequency Decomposition): A windowed Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) subsystem implemented via FFTW3 with single-precision floating-point arithmetic and ARM NEON SIMD vector extensions. It decomposes the \(10.0\text{ MHz}\) digitized bandwidth into \(N = 2048\) discrete spectral channels, achieving a fine spectral resolution of \(\Delta f \approx 4.8828\text{ kHz}\). 2. X-Engine (Cross-Multiplication & Calibration): A vectorized Cartesian cross-multiplication pipeline computing the complex instantaneous cross-power spectrum \(S_{12}[m]\), accompanied by simultaneous auto-power spectra \(S_{11}[m]\) and \(S_{22}[m]\). It incorporates sub-sample phase correction mechanisms for geometric fringe stopping and instrumental bandpass phase flattening. 3. Vector Accumulator (Welch Integration): A real-time time-integration engine operating with a 50% overlapping sliding window (hop size \(L = 1024\) samples). It coherently and radiometrically averages consecutive spectral frames across an integration interval \(\tau \approx 200\text{ ms}\) (\(M = 1953\) frames), suppressing uncorrelated Gaussian thermal noise by a factor of \(\sqrt{M}\) and compressing data throughput from \(80\text{ MB/s}\) to \(\sim 41.1\text{ KB/s}\). 4. Visibility Telemetry Streamer: A zero-copy, non-blocking POSIX UDP socket interface encapsulating the integrated power spectra into 8224-byte flat binary datagrams dispatched across local area networks to the visualizer client (viewer.py).

+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                  MODULE 3 FX CORRELATOR TOPOLOGY                                  |
|                                                                                                   |
|  [SHM Ring Buffer 1] ───> [ 50% Overlap ] ───> [ Hanning Window ] ───> [ FFTW3 F-Engine ] ──┐      |
|  (Aligned k = 0)          [ Slide Buffer]      [  w[n] Pre-calc ]      [ N = 2048 NEON  ]   │      |
|                                                                                             │      |
|                                                                        X1[m]                ▼      |
|                                                             ┌───────────────────────────> [ (X) ]  |
|                                                             │                             X-Engine |
|                                                             │  X2*[m]                       │      |
|  [SHM Ring Buffer 2] ───> [ 50% Overlap ] ───> [ Hanning Window ] ───> [ FFTW3 F-Engine ] ──┘      |
|  (Aligned k = 0)          [ Slide Buffer]      [  w[n] Pre-calc ]      [ N = 2048 NEON  ]          |
|                                                                                             │      |
|                                                                                  S12[m]     ▼      |
|                                                                            [ Fringe Stopping & Cal]|
|                                                                            [ S12 * exp(-j*Phi)     ]|
|                                                                                             │      |
|                                                                                             ▼      |
|  [ Telemetry UDP Streamer ] <─── [ FFT Shift ] <─── [ Normalization & dB ] <─── [ Welch Accumulator] |
|  (8224 B @ 5.0 Hz to LAN)        [ Index Shift]     [ 10*log10(|S12|+eps)]      [ M = 1953 Frames ] |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

The design targets four quantitative technical objectives: * Real-Time Continuous DSP Throughput: Continuous ingestion of dual 10.0 MSPS streams (\(80\text{ MB/s}\)) on a single ARM Cortex-A76 core of a Raspberry Pi 5 without sample drops or buffer overflows[cite: 1, 4]. * Fine Spectral & Temporal Resolution: Channel bandwidth \(\Delta f = 4.8828\text{ kHz}\) across \(N = 2048\) channels and time cadence \(\tau = 200\text{ ms}\) (\(M = 1953\) frames), optimized for tracking rapid solar radio burst frequency drifts[cite: 1, 4]. * Coherent Signal Detection & Radiometric Gain: Radiometric thermal noise suppression scaling as \(\sqrt{M}\) (\(> 14.9\text{ dB}\) improvement over single FFT frames, \(> 30\text{ dB}\) over raw samples), maintaining spatial coherence \(\gamma \ge 0.95\) on zero-baseline benchtop tests[cite: 1, 4]. * Low-Latency Telemetry Transport: Dispatch of packed 8224-byte UDP binary packets within \(1.6\text{ ms}\) after integration completion, with zero network blocking on the DSP core[cite: 1, 4].

docs.title: 1.2. Problem Formulation: Beyond Coarse Alignment to Astronomical Fringe Synthesis
1.2.1. Residual Sub-Sample Delay and Continuous Geometric Delay (\(\tau_g(t)\))
docs.text:
Module 2 addressed the gross asynchronous startup latency inherent to independent USB 3.0 controller enumeration by applying time-domain cross-correlation over snapshots of length \(N = 65536\) samples[cite: 1, 2, 9]. By executing a buffer skip operation (skip(k_offset)), Module 2 forced the discrete sample skew \(k_0 \in \mathbb{Z}\) to zero (\(|k| \le 1\text{ sample}\), or \(\le 100\text{ ns}\))[cite: 1, 2, 9]. However, this coarse alignment operates strictly at integer multiples of the sampling period \(T_s = 100\text{ ns}\)[cite: 1, 3, 7].

In astronomical radio interferometry, two outdoor antenna elements separated by an East-West baseline vector \(\mathbf{B}\) intercept celestial wavefronts arriving from an astronomical source (such as the Sun) at zenith angle \(\theta(t)\)[cite: 1, 7, 8]. The physical wavefront encounters a continuous path difference, creating an astronomical geometric delay[cite: 1, 7, 8]: $\(\tau_g(t) = \frac{\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{s}(t)}{c} = \frac{B \sin\theta(t)}{c} \tag{1}\)$ where \(c \approx 2.99792 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}\) is the speed of light in vacuum, \(B\) is the baseline baseline distance (\(10\text{ m} \le B \le 20\text{ m}\)), and \(\mathbf{s}(t)\) is the unit vector pointing toward the source[cite: 1, 7, 8].

Because the Earth rotates with diurnal angular velocity \(\omega_\oplus \approx 7.2921 \times 10^{-5}\text{ rad/s}\), the zenith angle \(\theta(t)\) and geometric delay \(\tau_g(t)\) are continuous real-valued functions of time[cite: 1, 7, 8]. The total time delay differential between the two receiver inputs is[cite: 7]: $\(\tau_{\text{total}}(t) = \tau_g(t) + \tau_{\text{inst}} + \Delta\tau_{\text{res}} \tag{2}\)$ where \(\tau_{\text{inst}}\) represents differential electrical delay along the RF feedlines and filters, and \(\Delta\tau_{\text{res}} \in (-T_s/2, +T_s/2)\) represents the residual uncompensated sub-sample delay remaining after Module 2's coarse integer sample alignment[cite: 1, 7]. By the Fourier time-shift property, a continuous time delay \(\Delta\tau\) manifests across the frequency domain as a linear phase slope[cite: 1, 7, 14]: $\(\frac{d(\Delta\phi)}{df} = 2\pi \Delta\tau \tag{3}\)$ Because \(\Delta\tau\) is fractional and time-varying, it cannot be eliminated by shifting discrete pointers in time-domain ring buffers[cite: 1, 3, 7].

docs.title: 1.2.2. Spectral Channelization vs. Fringe Washing (Decorrelation)
docs.text:
If two broadband signals exhibiting delay differential \(\tau\) are directly multiplied across the entire receiver bandwidth \(B_{\text{RF}} = 8.0\text{ MHz}\) without spectral decomposition, the resulting cross-correlation response suffers from severe decorrelation (commonly known as fringe washing)[cite: 1, 7, 8]. The integrated cross-power response across a continuous passband \([f_0 - B_{\text{RF}}/2, f_0 + B_{\text{RF}}/2]\) scales according to[cite: 1, 7, 8]: $\(R_{12}(\tau) = \int_{f_0 - B_{\text{RF}}/2}^{f_0 + B_{\text{RF}}/2} S(f) e^{j 2\pi f \tau} df = S_0 B_{\text{RF}} \cdot \text{sinc}(B_{\text{RF}} \tau) \cdot e^{j 2\pi f_0 \tau} \tag{4}\)$ where \(\text{sinc}(x) = \frac{\sin(\pi x)}{\pi x}\)[cite: 8]. For a full \(8.0\text{ MHz}\) analog bandwidth, the fringe pattern envelope contracts to a narrow width of \(\Delta\tau_{\text{null}} = \frac{1}{B_{\text{RF}}} = \frac{1}{8 \times 10^6\text{ Hz}} = 125\text{ ns}\)[cite: 1, 8]. On an interferometric baseline of \(B = 20\text{ m}\), the geometric delay varies over a range of \(\pm \frac{20\text{ m}}{3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}} \approx \pm 66.7\text{ ns}\)[cite: 1, 7]. If uncompensated, a fractional error of just \(60\text{ ns}\) attenuates the cross-correlation amplitude by more than \(50\%\) (\(\text{sinc}(8.0 \times 10^6 \times 60 \times 10^{-9}) \approx 0.68\))[cite: 1, 8].

The F-Engine overcomes fringe washing through narrow-band channelization[cite: 1, 7, 8]. By subdividing the digitized bandwidth into \(N = 2048\) discrete channels, each channel occupies a narrow spectral slice[cite: 1, 4]: $\(\Delta f = \frac{f_s}{N} = \frac{10.0\text{ MHz}}{2048} \approx 4882.8125\text{ Hz} \tag{5}\)$ Within any individual spectral channel \(m\), the phase dispersion across the bin is restricted to[cite: 1, 7, 8]: $\(\Delta\Phi_{\text{bin}} = 2\pi \Delta f \tau_g \le 2\pi \times (4.8828 \times 10^3\text{ Hz}) \times (66.7 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s}) \approx 2.05 \times 10^{-3}\text{ rad} \approx 0.117^\circ \tag{6}\)$ The fringe decorrelation factor within the bin evaluates to[cite: 1, 7, 8]: $\(\eta_{\text{fringe}} = \text{sinc}(\Delta f \tau_g) = \frac{\sin(\pi \times 4882.8 \times 66.7 \times 10^{-9})}{\pi \times 4882.8 \times 66.7 \times 10^{-9}} \ge 0.99983 \tag{7}\)$ This demonstrates that intra-bin decorrelation loss is strictly below \(0.02\%\) across the entire decametric observation band for baselines up to \(B \le 20\text{ m}\)[cite: 1, 7, 8]. Consequently, the interferometer can operate in both phase-tracked mode (fringe stopping) and uncompensated transit mode without loss of fringe visibility[cite: 1, 7, 8].

docs.title: 1.2.3. Instrumental Bandpass Phase Dispersion (\(\Delta\phi_0[m]\))
docs.text: In physical receiver hardware, the two analog signal chains exhibit independent transfer functions[cite: 1, 7, 12]: $\(H_1(f) = |H_1(f)| e^{j \phi_1(f)}, \quad H_2(f) = |H_2(f)| e^{j \phi_2(f)} \tag{8}\)$ These functions are shaped by analog intermediate frequency (IF) bandpass filters (\(8.0\text{ MHz}\) nominal bandwidth), low-noise amplifiers (LNAs), bias tees, and coaxial interconnects[cite: 1, 7, 12]. Due to manufacturing tolerances and component temperature coefficients, the differential group delay \(\tau_g(f) = -\frac{1}{2\pi} \frac{d\phi}{df}\) is non-uniform across the passband[cite: 1, 7]. This induces a static, frequency-dependent instrumental phase error[cite: 1, 7]: $\(\Delta\phi_0[m] = \phi_1(f_m) - \phi_2(f_m) \tag{9}\)$ Without measuring and applying this calibration vector, the reconstructed complex visibility phase will be warped, introducing artificial phase slopes and distorting the measured wavefront angles[cite: 1, 7, 14].

docs.title: 1.3. Scope and Quantitative Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
The scope of Module 3 encompasses baseband ingestion from shared memory, windowed forward Fourier decomposition via FFTW3, vectorized complex cross-multiplication, 50% overlapping Welch accumulation, logarithmic power conversion, and non-blocking UDP telemetry streaming[cite: 1, 4, 10]. Verification of Module 3 is bounded by four quantitative criteria[cite: 1]:

Metric Identifier Parameter Specification Target Value & Tolerance Verification Method CRIT-M3-01[cite: 1] Spectral Channel Resolution \(\Delta f = 4.8828\text{ kHz} \pm 0.001\text{ Hz}\)[cite: 1, 4] CW Tone Injection at \(+1.0\text{ MHz}\) (\(f = 36.0\text{ MHz}\)); peak must localize at exactly bin index 1229[cite: 1, 4, 7, 14]. CRIT-M3-02[cite: 1] Zero-Baseline Spatial Coherence \(\gamma(f) \ge 0.95\) across \(31.0\text{ MHz} - 39.0\text{ MHz}\)[cite: 1, 4, 14] Ingestion of common avalanche noise via 1:2 resistive splitter (\(\Delta L = 0\text{ cm}\))[cite: 1, 7, 11, 14]. CRIT-M3-03[cite: 1] Processing Latency per Hop \(T_{\text{proc}} \le 1.60\text{ ms}\) per 1024-sample block[cite: 1, 4] Benchmark execution timing on ARM Cortex-A76 core at 2.4 GHz; latency budget is \(102.4\ \mu\text{s} \times 1024 = 104.85\text{ ms}\) (safety margin \(> 60\times\))[cite: 1, 4]. CRIT-M3-04[cite: 1] Telemetry Packet Continuity Packet loss \(\le 0.001\%\), Cadence \(200\text{ ms} \pm 2\text{ ms}\)[cite: 1, 4] Continuous 60-second UDP datagram reception log over 1 Gbps LAN to viewer.py[cite: 1, 2, 4].

docs.title: 2. Physical Interconnect, Signal Environment & Calibration Topology
2.1. Dual-Regime Topology: Laboratory Calibration vs. Field Observation
docs.text:
Module 3 operates within two hardware interconnect regimes: laboratory calibration (zero-baseline benchtop) and astronomical field observation[cite: 1, 7, 11].

===================================================================================================
                               FIGURE 2.1: INTERCONNECT ROUTING
===================================================================================================
A. ZERO-BASELINE BENCHTOP CALIBRATION ROUTING
[ 2N2222 Noise Diode ]
[ Avalanche Source   ] ──> [ 1:2 Resistive Splitter ] ──┬──(Coax L1 = 1.0 m)──> [Port C] SDRplay #1
                            (3-Resistor Wye, 50 Ohm)    └──(Coax L2 = 1.0 m)──> [Port C] SDRplay #2
                                                                                       │
[ 24.0 MHz OCXO/RefGen] ───────────────────────────(T-Connector / Dual Ref)───────────┴──> [REFin Port]

B. FIELD INTERFEROMETRIC DUAL-ANTENNA ROUTING
[ West Dipole (Ant 1) ] ──> [ BPF 30-40 MHz ] ──> [ LNA/Bias-T ] ──> [ Switch RF1 ]
                                                                        [ HMC544AE   ] ──> [Port C] SDR #1
[ East Dipole (Ant 2) ] ──> [ BPF 30-40 MHz ] ──> [ LNA/Bias-T ] ──> [ Switch RF1 ]
                                                                        [ HMC544AE   ] ──> [Port C] SDR #2
                                                                               ▲
[ Noise Source Board  ] ──> [ 1:2 Splitter  ] ─────────────────────────> [ Switch RF2 ] (Calibration In)
                                                                               │
[ Raspberry Pi 5 GPIO ] ──────────────────────(Cal Control: HIGH/LOW)──────────┘
  1. Zero-Baseline Calibration Regime: A reverse-biased 2N2222 transistor operating in avalanche breakdown generates wideband Gaussian white noise with an excess noise ratio (\(ENR\)) exceeding \(30\text{ dB}\)[cite: 1, 2, 7, 11]. The output passes through a 10 dB attenuator pad and a symmetric 1:2 3-resistor Wye splitter (\(50\ \Omega\) impedance matched)[cite: 1, 7, 11]. Two RG-316 coaxial cables of identical electrical length (\(\Delta L = 0.0\text{ cm} \pm 0.1\text{ cm}\)) route the split signals into Port C (BNC) of the two RSPdx receivers[cite: 1, 2, 7, 11]. A shared 24.0 MHz reference clock drives both REFin ports to lock the ADC sampling clocks and eliminate phase drift[cite: 1, 2, 7]. This configuration establishes the zero-baseline state (\(\tau_g = 0\)) used to measure the static instrumental phase dispersion matrix \(\Delta\phi_0[m]\)[cite: 1, 7, 11].
  2. Field Observation Regime: Two broadband horizontal dipoles cut for \(35.0\text{ MHz}\) are deployed on an East-West baseline (\(B = 10\text{ m} - 20\text{ m}\))[cite: 1, 7, 11]. Each antenna path includes a 30–40 MHz bandpass filter (attenuating strong shortwave broadcast signals below 28 MHz and FM broadcast signals above 88 MHz) and an ultra-low-noise front-end preamplifier (FEE)[cite: 1, 7, 11]. High-isolation RF switches (HMC544AE) driven by Raspberry Pi 5 GPIO pins toggle between the antenna inputs and the internal noise source, enabling automated online phase calibration cycles without physical recabling[cite: 1, 7, 11].

docs.title: 2.2. Test Signal Behavior in the Frequency Domain: CW Tones vs. Broadband Noise
docs.text:
A fundamental contrast exists between the signal dynamics of Module 2 and Module 3[cite: 1, 7]:

Parameter / Dimension Module 2: Time-Domain Alignment (alignment_test)[cite: 1, 7] Module 3: Frequency-Domain FX Correlator (solar_correlator)[cite: 1, 7] Mathematical Domain Discrete Time Domain (\(R_{12}[k]\) via IFFT)[cite: 7, 14] Discrete Frequency Domain (\(S_{12}[m]\) via FFTW3)[cite: 1, 4, 7] Continuous Wave (CW) Tone FAILED / INVALID: Periodic sinusoidal correlation results in infinite cosine fringes; PNR saturates at \(3.92\text{ dB}\), causing timing ambiguity[cite: 1, 2, 7, 14]. OPTIMAL BENCHMARK: All signal power condenses into a single frequency bin \(f_0\); peak exceeds noise floor by \(> 50\text{ dB}\) with coherence \(\gamma \approx 1.0\)[cite: 1, 4, 7, 14]. Broadband Gaussian Noise OPTIMAL INPUT: Non-periodic noise collapses to a sharp Dirac delta peak \(\delta[k - k_0]\) with PNR \(\ge 44.0\text{ dB}\), enabling unambiguous sample alignment[cite: 1, 2, 7]. PASSBAND REFERENCE: Distributes energy uniformly across all 2048 bins, enabling bandpass gain profiling and phase matrix measurement \(\Delta\phi_0[m]\)[cite: 1, 7, 14]. Thermal Noise Floor Forms background variance limiting cross-correlation peak detection sensitivity[cite: 2, 7] Radiometrically suppressed via Welch accumulation across \(M\) frames by factor of \(\sqrt{M}\)[cite: 1, 4, 7]

During system startup, broadband noise is injected first so Module 2 can achieve coarse sample lock (\(k = 0\))[cite: 1, 7]. Once locked, CW tones can be injected to confirm channelization fidelity and verify spectral bin localization in Module 3[cite: 1, 7].

docs.title: 3.1. Mathematical Signal Model in Frequency Domain
docs.text:
Let the baseband voltage signals from the two receiver front-ends, following coarse alignment (\(k = 0\)), be modeled as complex discrete-time stochastic processes[cite: 1, 4, 7]: $\(x_1[n] = s_1[n] + w_1[n], \quad x_2[n] = s_2[n] + w_2[n] \tag{10}\)$ where \(w_1[n], w_2[n] \sim \mathcal{CN}(0, \sigma_w^2)\) represent independent, identically distributed circular complex Gaussian thermal noise processes generated by receiver LNAs and ADCs[cite: 1, 7].

In an interferometric deployment, the signals incident on the antennas contain contributions from the localized solar burst source \(s_{\text{sun}}(t)\), diffuse galactic synchrotron background radiation \(s_{\text{gal}}(t)\), and terrestrial radio frequency interference \(\text{rfi}(t)\)[cite: 1, 7, 12]. Passing these signals through the F-Engine channelizer yields the spectral representations at frequency bin \(m\) and time epoch \(t\)[cite: 1, 7, 12]: $\(X_1[m, t] = H_1[m] \Big( S_{\text{sun}}[m, t] + S_{\text{gal}, 1}[m, t] \Big) + \text{RFI}_1[m, t] + W_1[m, t] \tag{11}\)$ $\(X_2[m, t] = H_2[m] \Big( S_{\text{sun}}[m, t] e^{-j 2\pi f_m \tau_g(t)} + S_{\text{gal}, 2}[m, t] \Big) + \text{RFI}_2[m, t] + W_2[m, t] \tag{12}\)$ Here: * \(S_{\text{sun}}[m, t] \in \mathbb{C}\) is the complex analytic spectral amplitude of the solar emission[cite: 1, 7]. * \(f_m\) is the physical center frequency of bin \(m\)[cite: 1, 4, 7]. * \(\tau_g(t)\) is the geometric time delay between antennas along baseline \(\mathbf{B}\)[cite: 1, 7, 8]. * \(S_{\text{gal}, 1}, S_{\text{gal}, 2}\) are diffuse galactic noise components[cite: 1, 7, 12]. Because galactic emission is spatially extended across the hemisphere, it decorrelates on long baselines, yielding \(\langle S_{\text{gal}, 1} S_{\text{gal}, 2}^* \rangle \approx 0\)[cite: 7, 8, 12]. * \(W_1[m, t], W_2[m, t]\) are zero-mean Gaussian spectral noise variables satisfying \(\mathbb{E}[W_1 W_2^*] = 0\)[cite: 1, 7]. * \(H_1[m], H_2[m]\) represent the complex instrumental frequency response of channels 1 and 2[cite: 1, 7].

docs.title: 3.2. F-Engine Mechanics: Discrete Windowing & FFTW3 Spectral Decomposition
3.2.1. Windowing and Spectral Leakage Suppression (Symmetric Hanning)
docs.text:
Truncating continuous data into finite length blocks of size \(N = 2048\) is equivalent to applying a rectangular window, whose frequency response exhibits large sidelobes (first sidelobe at \(-13.2\text{ dB}\))[cite: 1]. In decametric observations, strong terrestrial transmitters (such as high-frequency broadcast stations) can leak across dozens of adjacent bins, obscuring weak astronomical solar bursts[cite: 1, 7].

To suppress spectral leakage, an analytic symmetric Hanning window \(w[n]\) is applied to each block prior to Fourier transformation[cite: 1, 4]: $\(w[n] = 0.5 \left[ 1 - \cos\left( \frac{2\pi n}{N - 1} \right) \right] = \sin^2\left( \frac{\pi n}{N - 1} \right), \quad n \in [0, N-1] \tag{13}\)$ The Hanning window suppresses the first sidelobe to \(-31.5\text{ dB}\) and accelerates asymptotic sidelobe roll-off to \(-18\text{ dB/octave}\) (compared to \(-6\text{ dB/octave}\) for rectangular windows)[cite: 1].

Windowing reduces total signal energy, requiring compensation via deterministic normalizations[cite: 1]: 1. Coherent Amplitude Normalization Factor (\(S_1\)): $\(S_1 = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} w[n] = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} \left[ 1 - \cos\left(\frac{2\pi n}{N-1}\right) \right] = \frac{N}{2} = 1024 \tag{14}\)$ 2. Equivalent Noise Energy Normalization Factor (\(S_2\)): $\(S_2 = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} w^2[n] = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} \frac{1}{4} \left[ 1 - 2\cos\left(\frac{2\pi n}{N-1}\right) + \cos^2\left(\frac{2\pi n}{N-1}\right) \right] \tag{15}\)$ Using the identity \(\cos^2(\theta) = \frac{1 + \cos(2\theta)}{2}\): $\(S_2 = \frac{1}{4} \left[ N - 0 + \frac{N}{2} \right] = \frac{3}{8} N = \frac{3}{8} \times 2048 = 768.0 \tag{16}\)$ \(S_2\) is applied downstream during Welch accumulation to ensure unscaled power estimates[cite: 1, 10].

docs.title: 3.2.2. Discrete Fourier Transform Implementation
docs.text: The windowed sequences \(\tilde{x}_1[n] = x_1[n] \cdot w[n]\) and \(\tilde{x}_2[n] = x_2[n] \cdot w[n]\) are transformed to the frequency domain via a 1D forward complex-to-complex DFT[cite: 1, 4]: $\(X[m] = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} \tilde{x}[n] \cdot e^{-j \frac{2\pi m n}{N}}, \quad m \in [0, N-1] \tag{17}\)$ With sampling frequency \(f_s = 10.0\text{ MSPS}\) and \(N = 2048\), the channel spacing is[cite: 1, 4]: $\(\Delta f = \frac{f_s}{N} = \frac{10.0 \times 10^6\text{ Hz}}{2048} = 4882.8125\text{ Hz} \tag{18}\)$ Following two-sided to centered frequency shifting (FFT Shift), the physical radio frequency corresponding to channel index \(m \in [0, 2047]\) with center frequency \(f_{\text{LO}} = 35.0\text{ MHz}\) is[cite: 1, 4]: $\(f_m = f_{\text{LO}} + \left( m - \frac{N}{2} \right) \Delta f = 35.0\text{ MHz} + (m - 1024) \times 4.8828125\text{ kHz} \tag{19}\)$ * Channel \(0\): \(f_0 = 35.0\text{ MHz} - 1024 \times 4882.8125\text{ Hz} = 30.000000\text{ MHz}\)[cite: 1, 5] * Channel \(1024\): \(f_{1024} = 35.000000\text{ MHz}\) (Direct Conversion DC / LO center)[cite: 1, 5] * Channel \(2047\): \(f_{2047} = 35.0\text{ MHz} + 1023 \times 4882.8125\text{ Hz} = 39.995117\text{ MHz}\)[cite: 1, 5]

docs.title: 3.3. X-Engine Mechanics: Cross-Multiplication, Auto-Power & Fringe Rotation
3.3.1. Complex Cross-Power Spectrum (\(S_{12}[m]\))
docs.text: At each frequency bin \(m\), the X-Engine computes the instantaneous complex cross-power spectrum by multiplying the complex spectrum of Channel 1 with the complex conjugate of Channel 2[cite: 1, 4]: $\(S_{12}[m] = X_1[m] \cdot X_2^*[m] \tag{20}\)$ Let \(X_1[m] = R_1[m] + j I_1[m]\) and \(X_2[m] = R_2[m] + j I_2[m]\), where \(R, I \in \mathbb{R}\)[cite: 1, 4]. The algebraic expansion is formulated as[cite: 1, 4]: $\(S_{12}[m] = (R_1 + j I_1)(R_2 - j I_2) = (R_1 R_2 + I_1 I_2) + j (I_1 R_2 - R_1 I_2) \tag{21}\)$ $\(\text{Re}(S_{12}[m]) = R_1[m] R_2[m] + I_1[m] I_2[m] \tag{22}\)$ $\(\text{Im}(S_{12}[m]) = I_1[m] R_2[m] - R_1[m] I_2[m] \tag{23}\)$ Decoupling into real scalar operations allows the C++ compiler to optimize execution using ARM NEON vector instructions (FMLA, FMLS) without pointer aliasing or complex-number overhead[cite: 1, 4, 10].

docs.title: 3.3.2. Auto-Power Spectra (\(S_{11}[m]\), \(S_{22}[m]\))
docs.text: Simultaneously, the X-Engine evaluates the real-valued auto-power spectra of both antennas to monitor channel integrity and enable downstream coherence normalization[cite: 1, 4]: $\(S_{11}[m] = \vert{}X_1[m]\vert{}^2 = X_1[m] X_1^*[m] = R_1^2[m] + I_1^2[m] \tag{24}\)$ $\(S_{22}[m] = \vert{}X_2[m]\vert{}^2 = X_2[m] X_2^*[m] = R_2^2[m] + I_2^2[m] \tag{25}\)$

docs.title: 3.3.3. Fringe Stopping & Phase Calibration API
docs.text:
To track astronomical sources across the sky and compensate for instrumental cable mismatches, the complex cross-power spectrum is corrected by applying an analytic phase rotation[cite: 1, 4]: $\(S_{12, \text{corrected}}[m] = S_{12}[m] \cdot e^{-j \Phi[m, t]} \tag{26}\)$ The composite phase correction angle \(\Phi[m, t]\) decomposes into two terms[cite: 1, 4]: $\(\Phi[m, t] = \Delta\phi_0[m] + 2\pi f_m \tau_g(t) \tag{27}\)$ where \(\Delta\phi_0[m]\) is the static calibration phase vector, and \(2\pi f_m \tau_g(t)\) is the geometric fringe stopping term[cite: 1, 4].

Expanding \(e^{-j \Phi} = \cos\Phi - j \sin\Phi\), the corrected real and imaginary visibility components evaluate to[cite: 1, 4]: $\(\text{Re}(S_{12, \text{corr}}) = \text{Re}(S_{12}) \cos\Phi + \text{Im}(S_{12}) \sin\Phi \tag{28}\)$ $\(\text{Im}(S_{12, \text{corr}}) = \text{Im}(S_{12}) \cos\Phi - \text{Re}(S_{12}) \sin\Phi \tag{29}\)$

The engine supports two operational observation modes[cite: 1, 7]: * Fringe Stopping Mode: The phase correction \(\Phi[m, t]\) is evaluated dynamically at every integration epoch using ephemeris coordinates for the Sun, locking the interferometer's synthetic fringe pattern to the source[cite: 1, 7]. * Transit Mode: Setting \(\tau_g(t) = 0\) leaves the geometric phase uncompensated, allowing the Sun to drift through the fixed primary antenna beam pattern and generating sinusoidal fringe oscillations[cite: 1, 7, 8]. The transit fringe period \(T_{\text{fringe}}\) is given by[cite: 2, 8]: $\(T_{\text{fringe}} = \frac{\lambda}{B \omega_\oplus \cos\delta} = \frac{c}{f_0 B \omega_\oplus \cos\delta} \tag{30}\)$ For \(f_0 = 35.0\text{ MHz}\) (\(\lambda \approx 8.565\text{ m}\)), an East-West baseline \(B = 15.0\text{ m}\), and solar declination \(\delta \approx 0^\circ\) (equinox): $\(T_{\text{fringe}} = \frac{8.565\text{ m}}{15.0\text{ m} \times (7.2921 \times 10^{-5}\text{ rad/s}) \times 1.0} \approx 7830.4\text{ s} \approx 130.5\text{ min} \tag{31}\)$

docs.title: 3.4. Time Integration (Welch's Method) & Statistical Radiometric Gain
3.4.1. 50% Overlap Welch Accumulation
docs.text: To achieve consistent spectral estimation, Module 3 implements Welch's Method of Averaged Modified Periodograms using a 50% overlap[cite: 1, 4, 10]. Consecutive FFT blocks advance by hop size \(L = 1024\) samples[cite: 1, 4, 10]. The number of overlapping frames \(M\) integrated within an interval \(\tau = 0.200\text{ s}\) (\(200\text{ ms}\)) at \(f_s = 10.0\text{ MSPS}\) is calculated as[cite: 1, 4, 10]: $\(M = \left\lfloor \frac{f_s \cdot \tau}{L} \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{10.0 \times 10^6 \times 0.200}{1024} \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{2,000,000}{1024} \right\rfloor = 1953\text{ frames} \tag{32}\)$ The time-averaged cross-power spectral estimator is[cite: 1, 4]: $\(\langle S_{12}[m] \rangle = \frac{1}{M \cdot S_2} \sum_{k=0}^{M-1} S_{12, k}[m] \tag{33}\)$ $\(\langle S_{11}[m] \rangle = \frac{1}{M \cdot S_2} \sum_{k=0}^{M-1} S_{11, k}[m], \quad \langle S_{22}[m] \rangle = \frac{1}{M \cdot S_2} \sum_{k=0}^{M-1} S_{22, k}[m] \tag{34}\)$ where \(S_2 = 768.0\) is the window energy normalization factor derived in Equation (16)[cite: 1, 10].

docs.title: 3.4.2. Noise Suppression and Radiometer Sensitivity Equation
docs.text:
Expanding the accumulated cross-power spectrum in terms of signal and noise components yields[cite: 1, 7]: $\(\langle S_{12}[m] \rangle = \frac{1}{M S_2} \sum_{k=0}^{M-1} \Big[ S_1[m, k] S_2^*[m, k] + S_1[m, k] W_2^*[m, k] + W_1[m, k] S_2^*[m, k] + W_1[m, k] W_2^*[m, k] \Big] \tag{35}\)$ Because \(W_1\) and \(W_2\) originate from independent receiver hardware chains, their cross-products have zero expectation[cite: 1, 7]: $\(\mathbb{E}\left[ \frac{1}{M} \sum_{k=0}^{M-1} W_1[m, k] W_2^*[m, k] \right] = 0 \tag{36}\)$ The variance of this accumulated noise sum decreases inversely with \(M\)[cite: 1, 7]: $\(\operatorname{Var}\left( \frac{1}{M} \sum_{k=0}^{M-1} W_1 W_2^* \right) = \frac{\sigma_{w1}^2 \sigma_{w2}^2}{M} \implies \sigma_{\text{cross}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}} \tag{37}\)$

According to the Ideal Radiometer Equation, the minimum detectable cross-correlated flux density (or equivalent system temperature sensitivity) scales as[cite: 1, 8]: $\(\Delta T_{\text{min}} = \frac{T_{\text{sys}}}{\sqrt{\Delta f \cdot \tau}} \tag{38}\)$ For channel bandwidth \(\Delta f = 4882.8125\text{ Hz}\) and integration time \(\tau = 0.200\text{ s}\)[cite: 1, 4]: $\(\sqrt{\Delta f \cdot \tau} = \sqrt{4882.8125 \times 0.200} = \sqrt{976.5625} = 31.25 \tag{39}\)$ $\(\Delta T_{\text{min}} = \frac{T_{\text{sys}}}{31.25} \tag{40}\)$ This integration yields a radiometric processing gain of[cite: 1]: $\(G_{\text{rad}} = 10 \log_{10}(31.25) \approx 14.9485\text{ dB} \tag{41}\)$ Relative to single-sample instantaneous fluctuations, the total processing gain across the \(2 \times 10^6\) raw samples ingested during each \(200\text{ ms}\) interval exceeds \(30\text{ dB}\)[cite: 1].

docs.title: 3.4.3. Normalized Complex Coherence (\(\gamma[m]\)) and Magnitude dB Conversion
docs.text:
The normalized complex coherence coefficient \(\gamma[m] \in [0, 1]\) measures the degree of correlation between the two antenna signals at each channel[cite: 1, 4]: $\(\gamma[m] = \frac{\big\vert{} \langle S_{12}[m] \rangle \big\vert{}}{\sqrt{\langle S_{11}[m] \rangle \cdot \langle S_{22}[m] \rangle}} \tag{42}\)$ * \(\gamma[m] = 1.0\): Fully coherent signal (ideal point source or common benchtop tone/noise source)[cite: 1, 7, 14]. * \(\gamma[m] = 0.0\): Completely uncorrelated signals (independent receiver thermal noise)[cite: 1, 7].

For visualization and data streaming, the cross-power magnitude is converted to a logarithmic decibel scale[cite: 1, 4]: $\(P_{\text{dB}}[m] = 10 \log_{10}\Big( \big\vert{} \langle S_{12}[m] \rangle \big\vert{} + \epsilon \Big) \tag{43}\)$ where \(\epsilon = 1.0 \times 10^{-12}\) is a small positive constant preventing numeric underflow and \(-\infty\) evaluation during zero-signal conditions[cite: 1, 4, 10]. Finally, the array undergoes an in-place cyclic shift (std::rotate or block swap) swapping bins \([0, 1023]\) and \([1024, 2047]\), aligning the physical center frequency (\(35.0\text{ MHz}\)) to array index 1024[cite: 1, 4, 10].

docs.title: 4.1. Zero-Allocation Hot-Loop Philosophy
docs.text:
At an ingest rate of \(10.0\text{ MSPS}\) per channel, the DSP pipeline processes one 1024-sample hop every \(102.4\ \mu\text{s}\)[cite: 1, 4]. Under this timing budget, invoking operating system heap management routines (malloc, free, new, realloc, or dynamically growing std::vector) in the execution loop is strictly prohibited[cite: 1, 10]. Dynamic memory management introduces lock contention and indeterminate latency spikes through kernel page allocation and heap consolidation, which risk overflowing the POSIX shared memory ring buffers[cite: 1, 10].

All required computational buffers—including the sliding window memory, window weight vectors, FFTW input/output structures, and accumulator arrays—are pre-allocated once during class instantiation within the FXCorrelator constructor[cite: 1, 10]. The inner processing loop operates strictly on static memory locations, maintaining deterministic instruction timings[cite: 1, 10].

docs.title: 4.2. 50% Overlapping Sliding Window Buffer Mechanics
docs.text:
To sustain a continuous 50% overlap without re-reading samples from shared memory, each receiver channel maintains an internal scratch buffer of size \(N = 2048\) samples (ComplexSample)[cite: 1, 10]:

===================================================================================================
                       FIGURE 4.1: 50% OVERLAPPING SLIDING WINDOW MECHANICS
===================================================================================================
T0 (Prime Phase):
[ Index 0 ........... 1023 ] [ Index 1024 ........... 2047 ]
[        Uninitialized     ] [ Pre-loaded HOP_SIZE Samples ] <─── rb.read(1024) in prime_buffers()

Cycle k (Shift & Ingest):
Step 1: Shift upper half to lower half (1024 samples) via std::memcpy:
        [ Index 0 ........... 1023 ] <==== [ Index 1024 ........... 2047 ]
Step 2: Read 1024 NEW samples from Ring Buffer into upper half:
        [ Index 0 ........... 1023 ]       [ Index 1024 ........... 2047 ] <─── rb.read(1024)
Step 3: Extract full contiguous block of N = 2048 samples:
        | <─────────────────────── FULL N = 2048 SAMPLES ────────────────────────> |
        Apply Hanning Window w[n] -> Cast int16 to float -> Execute FFTW Forward DFT
  1. Priming (prime_buffers()): Before initiating the correlation loop, 1024 samples are read from the shared memory ring buffer into indices \([1024, 2047]\) of the scratch buffer[cite: 1, 10].
  2. Shift and Load: At each hop iteration:
  3. The trailing 1024 samples are shifted forward: 
    std::memcpy(&slide_buf[0], &slide_buf[1024], 1024 * sizeof(ComplexSample));
  4. The next 1024 samples are read from the shared memory ring buffer into indices \([1024, 2047]\)[cite: 1, 10].
  5. This approach eliminates redundant memory transfers and guarantees that every 2048-sample FFT window advances by exactly \(L = 1024\) samples[cite: 1, 10].

docs.title: 4.3. ARMv8-A Cortex-A76 SIMD Optimization & FFTW3 Execution Engine
docs.text: The Raspberry Pi 5 is powered by a quad-core ARM Cortex-A76 processor operating at \(2.4\text{ GHz}\), supporting the ARMv8-A architecture with 128-bit NEON Advanced SIMD vector units[cite: 1, 10]. The DSP pipeline leverages these hardware capabilities through several design choices[cite: 1, 10]: * 64-Byte Cacheline Alignment: All dynamic FFT arrays are allocated using fftwf_alloc_complex(N), ensuring that base memory addresses align with 64-byte boundaries[cite: 1, 10]. This prevents unaligned memory penalties during 128-bit SIMD vector loads (VLD1.32) and stores (VST1.32)[cite: 1]. * Execution Plans (FFTW_MEASURE): FFT plans (fftwf_plan_dft_1d) are created during initialization using the FFTW_MEASURE flag[cite: 1, 10]. FFTW benchmarks multiple execution strategies directly on the Cortex-A76 pipeline, selecting optimal butterfly factorization trees tailored to the CPU's cache hierarchy before processing real data[cite: 1, 10]. * Contiguous Cartesian Vectorization: Arrays for real and imaginary components are organized contiguously in memory[cite: 1, 10]. When compiled with -O3 -march=native, the Cartesian cross-multiplication loops are automatically vectorized into NEON SIMD instructions, processing four single-precision floating-point values per instruction cycle[cite: 1, 10].

docs.title: 4.4. High-Performance Non-Blocking POSIX UDP Telemetry Engine
docs.text:
The telemetry engine streams integrated power spectra across the local network to remote display hosts without introducing stalls into the primary DSP thread[cite: 1, 4, 10].

The network packet layout uses strict single-byte structure packing (#pragma pack(push, 1)), avoiding compiler-inserted padding bytes across hardware platforms[cite: 1, 10]:

#pragma pack(push, 1)
struct TelemetryPacketHeader {
    char     magic[4];            // 4 Bytes: Ident identifier string "SOLR"
    uint64_t frame_id;            // 8 Bytes: Monotonically increasing frame sequence
    uint64_t timestamp_us;        // 8 Bytes: Microseconds since Unix epoch (UTC)
    uint32_t integration_frames;  // 4 Bytes: Constant value = 1953
    uint32_t payload_flags;       // 4 Bytes: Bitmask (Bit 0: dB Power Spectrum)
};                                // Total Header Size = 32 Bytes
#pragma pack(pop)

The datagram payload consists of \(N = 2048\) single-precision floating-point values (\(2048 \times 4\text{ bytes} = 8192\text{ bytes}\)) representing the centered decibel power spectrum[cite: 1, 10]. The total datagram size is: $\(\text{Packet Size} = 32\text{ bytes (Header)} + 8192\text{ bytes (Payload)} = 8224\text{ bytes} \tag{44}\)$

Key socket configuration details include[cite: 1, 10]: * Non-Blocking Operation: The socket descriptor is configured with the O_NONBLOCK file status flag via fcntl()[cite: 1, 10]. If network buffers become saturated, calls to sendto() return immediately with error code EWOULDBLOCK or EAGAIN rather than blocking the DSP thread[cite: 1, 10]. * Kernel Socket Buffer Expansion: The kernel transmit buffer (SO_SNDBUF) is set to \(1048576\text{ bytes}\) (\(1\text{ MB}\)) via setsockopt(), absorbing transient network stack delays without dropping frames[cite: 1, 10]. * Local MTU Handling: When traversing standard Ethernet networks with an MTU of 1500 bytes, IP fragmentation splits each 8224-byte packet into six fragments[cite: 1]. On gigabit LANs with standard switches, modern network stacks reassemble these fragments with packet drop rates below \(0.001\%\)[cite: 1]. Jumbo frame configurations (MTU 9000 bytes) can also be used to transmit the entire datagram within a single unfragmented Ethernet frame[cite: 1].

docs.title: 5.1. Source Code Modularization
docs.text:
The complete Module 3 source tree integrates directly into the existing repository structure[cite: 1, 10]:

solar_correlator/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Build configuration with -O3 -march=native
├── src/
│   ├── config.hpp              # Global system configuration constants
│   ├── ring_buffer.hpp         # SPSC Lock-free POSIX Shared Memory Ring Buffer
│   ├── time_alignment.hpp      # Module 2: TimeAligner class definition
│   ├── time_alignment.cpp      # Module 2: FFTW-based time-domain cross-correlator
│   ├── correlator.hpp          # Module 3: FXCorrelator class declaration
│   ├── correlator.cpp          # Module 3: F-Engine, X-Engine & Accumulator
│   ├── telemetry_sender.hpp    # Module 3: Non-blocking UDP streamer
│   └── main.cpp                # Master orchestration and signal handling
└── tests/
    ├── alignment_test.cpp      # Module 2 coarse alignment verification
    └── dsp_math_test.cpp       # Module 3 DSP numerical unit testbench
  • config.hpp: Centralizes configuration constants across the SDR, SHM, Alignment, Correlator, and Network namespaces[cite: 1, 10].
  • correlator.hpp / correlator.cpp: Implements the FXCorrelator class, managing the 50% overlap sliding buffers, pre-computed Hanning windows, FFTW plans, Cartesian cross-multipliers, and Welch accumulation arrays[cite: 1, 10].
  • telemetry_sender.hpp: Encapsulates non-blocking UDP transmission, frame serialization, and high-resolution POSIX timestamping[cite: 1, 10].
  • main.cpp: Manages overall lifecycle execution, coordinating the handover from Module 2 to Module 3 and handling POSIX system signals[cite: 1, 10].

docs.title: 5.2. Pipeline Transition: Handover from Module 2 to Module 3
docs.text:
The transition from coarse alignment to continuous correlation in main.cpp follows a two-phase initialization sequence[cite: 1, 10]:

===================================================================================================
                    FIGURE 5.1: MODULE 2 TO MODULE 3 PIPELINE HANDOVER
===================================================================================================
1. HARDWARE STARTUP & COARSE TIME ALIGNMENT (MODULE 2)
   main()
     │
     ├──> fork() ──> [ Producer Process Ch1 ] ──> Writes /shm_sdr_ch1 (10 MSPS)
     ├──> fork() ──> [ Producer Process Ch2 ] ──> Writes /shm_sdr_ch2 (10 MSPS)
     │
     ├──> Sleep 500 ms (Allow USB 3.0 Isochronous buffers to stabilize)
     ├──> Simultaneous Flush: rb1.flush(); rb2.flush();  <--- Chốt mốc T0
     │
     ├──> Snapshot Acquisition: N = 65,536 samples via rb.peek()
     ├──> TimeAligner::measure_offset() computes k_offset
     │
     └──> Coarse Alignment Execution:
             if (k_offset > 0) rb1.skip(k_offset);
             if (k_offset < 0) rb2.skip(-k_offset);
             Re-measure Snapshot: Assert(|k_new| <= 1 sample) ===> [PASS LOCKED]

2. CONTINUOUS FX CORRELATION TRANSITION (MODULE 3)
     │
     ├──> Maintain open POSIX shared memory file descriptors (Do NOT unlink)
     ├──> Pass live consumer tail pointers directly to FXCorrelator
     ├──> FXCorrelator::prime_buffers(rb1, rb2) loads initial 1024 samples
     │
     └──> Enter Infinite Hot Loop:
             while (g_running) {
                 correlator.process_cycle(rb1, rb2, sender, frame_id);
             }

By passing existing shared memory descriptors and tail pointers directly to FXCorrelator, no sample discontinuities or buffer reallocations occur during the handover[cite: 1, 10].

docs.title: 5.3. Real-Time Correlation Execution Loop (process_cycle())
docs.text:
The implementation of the correlation inner loop in correlator.cpp avoids heap allocations and optimizes SIMD execution[cite: 1, 10]:

bool FXCorrelator::process_hop(SharedMemoryRingBuffer& rb1, 
                               SharedMemoryRingBuffer& rb2) 
{
    // 1. Shift upper half of sliding scratch buffers to lower half
    std::memcpy(&slide_ch1_[0], &slide_ch1_[HOP_SIZE], HOP_SIZE * sizeof(ComplexSample));
    std::memcpy(&slide_ch2_[0], &slide_ch2_[HOP_SIZE], HOP_SIZE * sizeof(ComplexSample));

    // 2. Ingest 1024 new samples from shared memory ring buffers
    while (rb1.available_read() < HOP_SIZE || rb2.available_read() < HOP_SIZE) {
        if (!g_running) return false;
        std::this_thread::yield();
    }
    rb1.read(&slide_ch1_[HOP_SIZE], HOP_SIZE);
    rb2.read(&slide_ch2_[HOP_SIZE], HOP_SIZE);

    // 3. F-Engine: Apply pre-computed Hanning window & convert int16 to float
    for (uint32_t n = 0; n < FFT_SIZE; ++n) {
        const float w = hanning_window_[n];
        fft_in_ch1_[n][0] = static_cast<float>(slide_ch1_[n].i) * w;
        fft_in_ch1_[n][1] = static_cast<float>(slide_ch1_[n].q) * w;
        fft_in_ch2_[n][0] = static_cast<float>(slide_ch2_[n].i) * w;
        fft_in_ch2_[n][1] = static_cast<float>(slide_ch2_[n].q) * w;
    }

    // 4. Execute 1D Forward FFTs via FFTW3 NEON kernels
    fftwf_execute(fft_plan_ch1_);
    fftwf_execute(fft_plan_ch2_);

    // 5. X-Engine: Cartesian Cross-Multiplication & Auto-Power Accumulation
    for (uint32_t m = 0; m < FFT_SIZE; ++m) {
        const float r1 = fft_out_ch1_[m][0];
        const float i1 = fft_out_ch1_[m][1];
        const float r2 = fft_out_ch2_[m][0];
        const float i2 = fft_out_ch2_[m][1];

        // Complex cross product: S12 = X1 * conj(X2)
        const float cross_r = r1 * r2 + i1 * i2;
        const float cross_i = i1 * r2 - r1 * i2;

        accum_cross_real_[m] += cross_r;
        accum_cross_imag_[m] += cross_i;
        accum_auto_ch1_[m]   += (r1 * r1 + i1 * i1);
        accum_auto_ch2_[m]   += (r2 * r2 + i2 * i2);
    }

    ++frames_accumulated_;
    return true;
}

bool FXCorrelator::finalize_integration(std::vector<float>& spectrum_db_out) {
    if (frames_accumulated_ < INTEGRATION_FRAMES) return false;

    const float norm_factor = 1.0f / (static_cast<float>(frames_accumulated_) * WINDOW_S2);

    for (uint32_t m = 0; m < FFT_SIZE; ++m) {
        const float cr = accum_cross_real_[m] * norm_factor;
        const float ci = accum_cross_imag_[m] * norm_factor;
        const float magnitude = std::sqrt(cr * cr + ci * ci);

        // Convert magnitude to logarithmic decibels
        uncentered_db_[m] = 10.0f * std::log10(magnitude + DYNAMIC_RANGE_EPS);
    }

    // Two-sided to centered frequency shifting (FFT Shift)
    // Swap lower half [0, 1023] and upper half [1024, 2047]
    const uint32_t half = FFT_SIZE / 2;
    std::memcpy(&spectrum_db_out[0],    &uncentered_db_[half], half * sizeof(float));
    std::memcpy(&spectrum_db_out[half], &uncentered_db_[0],    half * sizeof(float));

    // Reset accumulators for next integration cycle
    std::fill(accum_cross_real_.begin(), accum_cross_real_.end(), 0.0f);
    std::fill(accum_cross_imag_.begin(), accum_cross_imag_.end(), 0.0f);
    std::fill(accum_auto_ch1_.begin(),   accum_auto_ch1_.end(),   0.0f);
    std::fill(accum_auto_ch2_.begin(),   accum_auto_ch2_.end(),   0.0f);
    frames_accumulated_ = 0;

    return true;
}

docs.title: 5.4. Thread Lifecycle, POSIX Signal Handling & Clean Teardown
docs.text:
To prevent shared memory leaks and driver deadlocks upon termination, main.cpp installs POSIX signal handlers for SIGINT and SIGTERM[cite: 1, 10]: 1. Signal Interception: The signal handler toggles an atomic flag: 

std::atomic<bool> g_running{true};
2. Loop Termination: The primary DSP execution loop detects g_running == false and exits cleanly[cite: 1, 10]. 3. Child Process Termination: The parent process issues kill(pid, SIGTERM) to both SDRplay producer processes and awaits process termination using waitpid()[cite: 1, 10]. 4. Hardware and Memory Cleanup: FFT plans are destroyed (fftwf_destroy_plan), SIMD buffers are deallocated (fftwf_free), UDP sockets are closed, and shared memory segments are unmapped and removed via shm_unlink()[cite: 1, 10].

docs.title: 6.1. Multi-Stage Verification Methodology
docs.text: System qualification uses a four-stage verification methodology[cite: 1]: * Stage 0: Handover Verification: Validates that Module 2 achieves sample lock (\(k = 0\)) and maintains PNR \(\ge 40\text{ dB}\) before activating the correlator[cite: 1, 2]. * Stage 1: Synthetic CW Tone Test: Injecting a synthetic \(+1.0\text{ MHz}\) complex exponential (\(x[n] = e^{j 2\pi (1.0/10.0) n}\)) into both channels tests spectral bin localization[cite: 1, 4, 7, 14]. For \(f_{\text{offset}} = +1.0\text{ MHz}\), \(f_s = 10.0\text{ MSPS}\), and \(N = 2048\), the target bin index evaluates to[cite: 4, 7, 14]: $\(\text{bin}_{\text{peak}} = 1024 + \frac{1.0\text{ MHz}}{10.0\text{ MHz} / 2048} = 1024 + 204.8 \approx 1229 \tag{45}\)$ The peak must localize at bin 1229 with coherence \(\gamma \ge 0.99\)[cite: 1, 4, 7, 14]. * Stage 2: Independent Noise Suppression Test: Independent pseudo-random Gaussian noise streams are injected into Channel 1 and Channel 2[cite: 1, 4, 7, 14]. The integrated cross-power must decrease relative to the auto-power by a factor scaling as \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{M}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1953}} \approx \frac{1}{44.19}\) (an attenuation of \(\approx 16.45\text{ dB}\))[cite: 1, 4, 7, 14]. * Stage 3: Zero-Baseline Hardware Benchtop Run: Common avalanche noise is fed through a 1:2 resistive splitter into both receivers[cite: 1, 7, 11, 14]. The measured coherence across the active passband (\(31 - 39\text{ MHz}\)) must satisfy \(\gamma(f) \ge 0.95\), while the cross-power phase \(\Delta\phi(f)\) must remain flat within \(\pm 2^\circ\)[cite: 1, 4, 14]. * Stage 4: 60-Second Real-Time Telemetry Benchmark: The full system runs continuously for 60 seconds, streaming telemetry to viewer.py[cite: 1, 2, 10]. Verification requires zero dropped buffers, steady CPU load, and stable transmission cadences (\(200\text{ ms} \pm 2\text{ ms}\))[cite: 1, 4].

docs.text: Bản vá dựa trên commit 7b78ef472d416b0de6a721ef21aa35958f39a5c8 của https://github.com/tuchau1404/solar_correlator, clone sạch ngày 16/10/2026. Không có thay đổi cục bộ trong checkout lúc bắt đầu. Không push và không chạy phần cứng.

docs.title: Kết quả đọc code trước khi sửa
docs.text:
Đã đọc src/main.cpp, config.hpp, network_config.hpp, telemetry_sender.hpp, correlator.hpp/.cpp, viewer/telemetry_protocol.py, viewer_fx.py, các test telemetry/viewer và CMake.

Correlator tính X1*conj(X2), tích phân visibility phức, rồi áp dụng vector pha phi theo thứ tự FFT chưa shift. Các đầu ra đã được fftshift qua j=(k+N/2)%N. Main chỉ đổi auto-power tuyến tính sang dB; không fftshift lần nữa.

  • S12_dB = 10 log10(max(|S12|, 1e-12)).
  • S11_dB, S22_dB lấy từ auto-power đã chuẩn hóa ADC-count²/bin.
  • Phase = atan2(Im(S12), Re(S12)), radian; bao gồm phép bù phi đang có.
  • Coherence amplitude gamma = |S12| / (sqrt(S11)*sqrt(S22)), clamp 0–1. Không phải gamma². Power bằng 0 cho phase/coherence bằng 0 nhưng đó là ước lượng invalid.
  • Tần số bin j: 30 + j*10/2048 MHz. Bin 1126 = 35.498046875 MHz.
  • Công suất là dB re 1 ADC-count²/bin, không phải dBm hoặc SFU.
  • Header v2 có 52 byte, flags luôn 1, mỗi đối tượng sender tạo một session riêng. Vì thế v2 không tự mô tả phase/coherence hoặc phân biệt S11/S22/S12.

Các file thuật toán/hardware bị giới hạn trong yêu cầu không được sửa.

docs.title: Hợp đồng SOL2 v3 cuối cùng
docs.text:
Tất cả integer và IEEE-754 float32 dùng big endian. Mỗi datagram có 52 byte header và 256 float32, tổng 1076 byte UDP payload; 8 datagram cho một phổ 2048 bin. Không truyền ABI struct. Không thay nghĩa v2: backend main dùng version 3.

Offset byte Kiểu Ý nghĩa 0 4 byte ASCII SOL2 4 uint16 Version = 3 6 uint16 Header bytes = 52 8 uint64 Session ngẫu nhiên, khác 0; main tạo một lần và chia sẻ cả năm sender 16 uint64 Frame ID, từ 0; cùng cycle dùng cùng ID; cycle bị bỏ để lại gap nếu tiếp tục phục hồi 24 uint64 UTC Unix microseconds, lấy một lần sau khi cycle DSP hoàn tất; không phải hardware sample timestamp 32 uint32 Integration frames = 1953 36 uint32 Flags = 1 | (payload_type << 8); bit 0 = fftshifted; mọi bit khác ngoài vùng type phải bằng 0 40 uint16 Total bins = 2048 42 uint16 Chunk index 0–7 44 uint16 Chunks per frame = 8 46 uint16 Bins in this chunk = 256 48 uint32 Bin offset = chunk index × 256 52 256 × float32 Payload của chunk Type Flags Cổng mặc định Payload 1 0x101 9999 Cross-power magnitude S12, dB 2 0x201 9998 Auto-power S11, dB 3 0x301 9997 Auto-power S22, dB 4 0x401 9996 Cross-phase rad, −π đến +π 5 0x501 9995 Coherence amplitude gamma, 0–1

V3 hiện cố định N=2048, M=1953, hop=1024, fs=10 MHz và RF center=35 MHz. Không có metadata tần số/cadence tùy biến trên wire. Khi thay cấu hình DSP phải cập nhật hợp đồng/receiver trước. Metadata giữa các luồng phải khớp timestamp và integration count chính xác.

Main gửi cả phase và coherence từ cùng vector kết quả cycle; không tính lại DSP, không log10 phase/coherence. Đường kiểm tra cycle/overflow/producer và fail-closed vẫn nằm trước mọi send. Thay đổi ngoài CLI/send chỉ là tăng telemetry frame ID khi cycle bị bỏ, để lịch sử không nối qua lần phục hồi chẩn đoán.

Sender dùng socket nonblocking, MSG_DONTWAIT, PMTU-discovery và không retry trong đường send. Giữ thống kê attempted, queued, failed, datagrams, invalid, would_block, no_buffers, too_large, interrupted, other, last_errno. queued chỉ có nghĩa kernel nhận đủ 8 datagram, không có xác nhận delivery.

docs.title: Receiver, ghép frame và giới hạn bộ nhớ
docs.text:
Receiver(..., expected_type=T) chỉ nhận v3 đúng loại T; cổng chỉ định vị socket, header mới là nguồn nhận diện loại dữ liệu. Sai type/version hiện lỗi trong status bar và tăng counter, không chuyển sang cách diễn giải khác. Receiver không sửa số liệu invalid.

  • Reassembly: tối đa 8 frame dở dang mỗi luồng, timeout 0.75 s theo monotonic clock. Chấp nhận chunk đảo thứ tự, duplicate giống nhau; duplicate khác nội dung bị loại/quarantine. V3 cho phép frame hoàn tất đảo thứ tự trong cửa sổ 8 frame; giữ 64 ID hoàn tất gần nhất.
  • Mỗi receiver có queue 300 frame, tràn queue bỏ frame hiển thị cũ và tăng display_skips.
  • Join cache: tối đa 32 key (session, frame ID), grace period 0.35 s. S12 quyết định session đang hiển thị. Giữ tối đa 32 session cũ để loại gói trễ.
  • UI nạp xen kẽ các queue theo timestamp/frame; không ghép các bản “latest” theo cổng. Có đủ luồng thì xuất ngay; hết grace thì xuất S12 và những luồng có metadata khớp. Luồng thiếu không chặn UI, không mượn coherence frame trước. Luồng không có S12 hết hạn bị bỏ.
  • Một frame đã xuất không được AUX đến trễ sửa lại. Frame trễ hơn ID đã xuất bị bỏ. Khi quá giới hạn cache, frame cũ bị loại; gap thể hiện trong lịch sử.
  • Session mới reset lịch sử, deep accumulator và mốc frame; không ghép khác session.
  • Lịch sử waterfall S12/phase/coherence giới hạn 300 slot; time trace giữ tối đa 9003 bản ghi scalar tại bin chọn (khoảng 30 phút ở cadence danh định). Gap rất dài chỉ chèn đến giới hạn từng bộ đệm. Bộ nhớ không tăng theo thời gian chạy.

Counter frame_gaps ở reassembler là số gap quan sát lúc hoàn tất frame tiến tới; frame hoàn tất trễ có thể lấp gap nên đây không phải thống kê mất gói cuối cùng. UDP không có authentication/retransmission; tùy chọn --source-ip lọc nguồn IP.

docs.title: Viewer CW và Solar
docs.text:
Mặc định CW, chọn 35.5 MHz và làm tròn về bin gần nhất. Không tự bám peak. Click phổ hoặc nhập MHz; GUI hiện tần số yêu cầu, bin và tần số thực tế. Đổi lựa chọn xóa time trace; waterfall toàn dải vẫn được giữ.

  • Time trace: phase wrapped độ, −180° đến +180°, coherence cùng bin/frame. Trục thời gian dùng UTC timestamp nhận được, nhãn Vietnam UTC+07:00. Chèn NaN qua gap, phase invalid, bước wrap >180°, thời gian lùi hoặc gap thời gian lớn hơn 1.5 cadence danh định. Không unwrap và không làm mượt pha.
  • Mask: cần phase và gamma khớp frame, hữu hạn, gamma >0 và gamma ≥ ngưỡng hiển thị. Gamma=0 luôn invalid kể cả ngưỡng đặt 0. Thiếu gamma thì phase trống.
  • Waterfall pha và S12 dùng cùng bin, frame slot và nhãn UTC+7 lấy từ timestamp từng frame. Đây là trục frame slot có nhãn thời gian, không phải phép nội suy lên lưới UTC đều. Gap không có timestamp được để trống. Hai đầu bảng màu pha −180°/+180° cùng màu. NaN được render trong suốt, không biến thành pha 0°.
  • Solar hiện thêm waterfall pha và waterfall S12 trung bình sâu. CW ưu tiên time trace. Có thể chuyển mode trong GUI. S11/S22 chỉ overlay nếu khớp observation hiện tại.
  • Các colorbar công suất chỉnh được. Ngưỡng gamma mặc định 0.5 chỉ phục vụ hiển thị, không được dùng như chuẩn nghiệm thu solar burst.
  • Deep S12 giữ phép trung bình miền công suất tuyến tính từ |S12| rồi đổi về dB. Không phải coherent integration visibility, không trung bình góc wrapped.

docs.title: Build và chạy
docs.text:
Trên Pi đã cài SDK SDRplay, FFTW3 single precision và pkg-config:

cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSOLAR_NATIVE=ON
cmake --build build -j4

Thay 192.168.1.2 bằng IPv4 máy viewer. Các lệnh sau là hướng dẫn, chưa chạy trên Pi. Giữ quy trình alignment/calibration hiện hữu; chế độ GUI không thay chế độ hardware.

Backend cho cả CW và solar (mặc định năm cổng như bảng):

./build/solar_correlator --dest-ip 192.168.1.2 \
  --port-s12 9999 --port-s11 9998 --port-s22 9997 \
  --port-phase 9996 --port-coherence 9995

Viewer trên máy nhận:

python -m pip install -r viewer/requirements.txt
python viewer/viewer_fx.py --mode cw --frequency-mhz 35.5 --coherence-threshold 0.5 --time-window 120
python viewer/viewer_fx.py --mode solar --frequency-mhz 35.5 --coherence-threshold 0.5

CW bỏ alignment chỉ trong quy trình chẩn đoán đã chủ động chọn: backend thêm --skip-align; GUI vẫn --mode cw. Không dùng cờ đó như mặc định quan trắc. Muốn phase calibration, dùng cờ --cal-phase đang có sau khi lựa chọn quy trình phù hợp; backend vẫn cấm kết hợp --skip-align và --cal-phase như trước.

S11/S22/phase/coherence có thể tắt bằng port 0 ở cả hai phía. S12 bắt buộc 1..65535; mọi cổng bật phải khác nhau. Nếu tắt coherence, S12 vẫn chạy, nhưng phase bị mask hoàn toàn.

docs.title: Chuyển từ v2 / CLI cũ
docs.text:
--port-aux và --aux-mode bị từ chối bằng thông báo chuyển đổi rõ ràng ở cả main và viewer FX. Dùng --port-phase và --port-coherence; cập nhật backend và viewer cùng lúc. Không có auto-detect hoặc fallback v2 trong viewer FX mới.

Để tránh phá công cụ cũ, constructor C++ hai tham số TelemetrySender(ip, port) vẫn phát v2 flags=1. Các tool test/dual-waterfall cũ và viewer.py, viewer_dual.py tiếp tục đường legacy này, được test riêng. Main mới gọi constructor có session/type nên phát v3. Không gửi phase/coherence qua constructor legacy và không ghép các session v2 độc lập.

docs.title: File thay đổi
docs.text:
File Lý do src/main.cpp CLI hai cổng, session chung, gửi năm vector cùng cycle; frame gap khi cycle bị bỏ src/network_config.hpp Cổng phase/coherence mặc định src/telemetry_sender.hpp Typed v3 và session do main cấp, giữ constructor legacy v2 viewer/telemetry_protocol.py Decode type/version, cache ghép frame, restart và giới hạn bộ nhớ viewer/science_model.py (mới) Mô hình lịch sử, chọn bin, mask pha, ngắt wrap/gap viewer/viewer_fx.py GUI CW/Solar, time trace, waterfall pha, điều khiển mask và tần số tests/test_telemetry_sender.cpp Header v2/v3, đồng nhất năm loại, nonblocking/no-allocation, errno counters tests/test_protocol_v3.py (mới) Reassembly, type/version, loss, duplicate, timeout, restart, metadata, session isolation tests/test_science_viewer.py (mới) CW/burst, wrap/gap/bin, memory bounds, GUI offscreen/alpha/color/geometry/click tests/send_v3_fixture.cpp (mới) Sender năm luồng giả lập, không hardware tests/test_udp_v3.py (mới) C++ → UDP → Python → GUI, CW/burst/restart CMakeLists.txt Thêm executable fixture để kiểm thử tích hợp C++/Python; không thêm dependency docs/02-firmware-dsp/telemetry-v3-upgrade.md Hợp đồng, sử dụng, giới hạn và bàn giao docs/02-firmware-dsp/module4-telemetry.md, viewer-modes.md Dẫn tới hợp đồng mới, đánh dấu tài liệu cũ không dùng cho v3

src/config.hpp được đọc nhưng không cần sửa; UDP_PORT_AUX cũ còn để tương thích nguồn. viewer/requirements.txt giữ nguyên.

docs.title: Kiểm thử có thể chạy lại không cần SDR
docs.text:
cmake -S . -B build -DSOLAR_BUILD_HARDWARE=OFF -DSOLAR_BUILD_DSP=OFF
cmake --build build -j2
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  SENDER_BINARY=./build/test_udp_sender V3_SENDER_BINARY=./build/send_v3_fixture \
  python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v

Kết quả thực chạy nằm trong VALIDATION.txt của gói bàn giao. Môi trường kiểm tra: Linux x86_64, GCC 13.3.0, Python 3.12, NumPy 2.3.5, PyQt5 5.15.11, Qt 5.15.19 và PyQtGraph 0.13.7. Build UDP-only bằng CMake; main còn được biên dịch/liên kết riêng với SDK SDRplay 3.15 và thư viện FFTW có sẵn, chạy help/CLI sai trước đường hardware. Compiler cảnh báo sẵn có trong hardware_control.hpp về bỏ qua return value system(); file này không được sửa.

Các kiểm thử bao phủ 11 nhóm yêu cầu: năm payload cùng định danh; sai version/type; đảo/mất/trùng chunk/timeout; restart frame 0 session mới; không ghép coherence n−1; CW một bin với pha nhiễu ở bin khác; wrap/gap/đổi bin; thiếu coherence vẫn có S12; NaN mask render alpha 0; burst dịch tần pha biết trước; cache/history có giới hạn. Có kiểm tra backlog 80 frame và click chọn tần số. Đã xem ảnh GUI offscreen ở hai mode.

Chưa xác minh Windows, Pi 5/ARM, SDRplay streaming thật, mạng giữa Pi và PC, hiệu năng dài hạn, path MTU thực tế, calibration vật lý hoặc quan trắc solar burst thật. Chưa có tiêu chí chất lượng khoa học ngoài mask hiển thị, chưa hỗ trợ unwrap, chưa có per-bin flags chất lượng hardware. Không thêm nhãn dBm/SFU.

docs.title: Cập nhật CW live view sau kiểm tra hiển thị pha (16/10/2026)
docs.text:
Đã tái hiện lỗi khung nhìn: sau khi người dùng zoom/pan trục thời gian, dữ liệu vẫn cập nhật nhưng view có thể giữ vùng thời gian cũ. Thử nghiệm có 80 điểm pha hợp lệ, 0 điểm nằm trong view cũ; đặt lại view thấy đủ 80 điểm. Điều này không chứng minh mọi trường hợp pha trống trên máy thật đều có cùng nguyên nhân.

Bản cập nhật chỉ sửa viewer/model/test/tài liệu, không cần build lại backend v3:

  • Time window (s) chọn 15–1800 giây; mặc định 120 giây; CLI --time-window 600 chọn 10 phút. Số liệu lịch sử chỉ được thu từ lúc viewer chạy/chọn bin.
  • Follow live mặc định bật, đặt trục X phase/coherence theo timestamp mới nhất kể cả khi pha bị mask. Kéo/zoom thủ công trên đồ thị thời gian tắt Follow live.
  • Reset time view bật lại bám thời gian và đặt Y phase −180..180°, gamma 0..1.05.
  • Dòng số đo hiện phase nhận được tại bin chọn bằng độ và rad, gamma cùng frame, frame ID, timestamp và VALID/MASKED kèm lý do. Phase nhận được vẫn có thể hiện dạng số với nhãn MASKED; nó không được đưa vào đường pha chất lượng hợp lệ. Thiếu dữ liệu hiện missing/waiting, không thay bằng 0°.
  • Coherence tiếp tục hiện khi dưới ngưỡng mask pha. Không dùng mask pha để ngắt mọi cặp mẫu coherence thành các đoạn một điểm không nhìn thấy.
  • Time trace dài chỉ lưu scalar selected-bin phase/coherence cùng metadata; không giữ năm phổ 2048 bin cho mỗi điểm trong 30 phút. Waterfall vẫn 300 slot.
  • Đổi bin/session vẫn xóa trace, không trộn dữ liệu. Không thay thuật toán tính pha, không thay mốc calibration, không làm mượt và không unwrap.

Kiểm thử bổ sung: chuyển phase +67.4° → −1.15° trong đồ thị và số đo; view mới chứa sample mới nhất; thời lượng 600/1800 giây; pause/resume qua nút Reset; dữ liệu scalar và cache hữu hạn; coherence liên tục khi phase bị mask; thiếu gamma không báo 0°. Đã xem ảnh GUI CW offscreen. Chưa kiểm thử tương tác trên Windows hoặc UDP từ Pi thật.

docs.title: Viewer modes
docs.text: SOL2 v3 update (2026-10-16): Main và viewer FX hiện dùng năm luồng typed v3. Xem hợp đồng, lệnh chạy và kiểm thử mới. Phần nội dung cũ bên dưới không phải hợp đồng hoặc hướng dẫn chạy v3.

docs.title: Solar Correlator Visualization Modes & Execution Guide
docs.text: This document details the telemetry architecture, operational display modes, plot configurations, and execution commands for the real-time visualization suite of the Decametric Solar Radio Interferometer (30.0 – 40.0 MHz).

docs.title: 1. Telemetry Architecture Overview
docs.text: The visualization clients run on the Host Workstation / PC and ingest binary UDP datagrams transmitted from the Raspberry Pi 5 Edge DSP Backend across the local network: * Operating Frequency Band: 30.0 MHz to 40.0 MHz (\(f_{\text{center}} = 35.0\text{ MHz}\), \(\text{Bandwidth} = 10.0\text{ MHz}\)). * Frequency Channels: 2048 bins (channel resolution \(\Delta f \approx 4.8828\text{ kHz}\)). * Nominal Cadence: \(200\text{ ms} \pm 2\text{ ms}\) per frame (\(5\text{ FPS}\), corresponding to \(M = 1953\) to \(2441\) integrated FFT frames). * Datagram Payload: 8,220 bytes total (28-byte packed header with SOLR identifier, monotonic Frame ID, microsecond timestamp, followed by 2048 IEEE 754 float32 decibel values). * Power Calibration Unit: \(\text{dB re 1 ADC-count}^2/\text{bin}\) (nominal dynamic range \(10.0\text{ dB}\) to \(95.0\text{ dB}\)). * Time System: All GUI title bars convert raw microsecond UTC timestamps into Vietnam Time (ICT / UTC+7, format: HH:MM:SS.mmm).

docs.title: 2. Comprehensive Visualization Modes
docs.text: The project provides three distinct visualization scripts tailored for specific observational, diagnostic, and calibration workflows:

docs.title: Mode 1: Standard Science Observation (viewer/viewer.py)
docs.text:
• Primary Target: Routine solar transit observations, coronal mass ejection tracking, and scientific solar radio burst monitoring (Solar Type II and Type III sweeps).
  • Backend Pipeline: solar_correlator daemon executing Module 2 (hardware time-alignment lock at \(k=0\)) followed by Module 3 (FX Correlator).
  • Network Channels: Listens on a single UDP socket (0.0.0.0:9999).
  • Display Layout (2 Stacked Panels):
  • Top Panel (1D Spectrum): Real-time cross-power spectrum \(|S_{12}(f)|\) plotted in bright yellow (#ffdc32) across 30.0 – 40.0 MHz. Displays dynamic peak tracking (dB amplitude and MHz center frequency) and frame metadata in the header.
  • Bottom Panel (2D Waterfall): Rolling 300-frame time-frequency spectrogram (~60 seconds history at \(200\text{ ms/slot}\)) using the high-contrast inferno colormap. Includes an interactive ColorBarItem / HistogramLUTItem on the right for mouse-dragged dynamic range adjustments (default \(20.0\text{ dB}\) to \(85.0\text{ dB}\)).

docs.title: Mode 2: Hardware Diagnostic & RF Bench Split-View (viewer/viewer_dual.py)
docs.text:
• Primary Target: Hardware validation, bench testing with RF splitters, coaxial cable matching, and real-time gain calibration between the two RSPdx receivers without running cross-correlation or Module 2 time alignment.
  • Backend Pipeline: tests/dual_waterfall_test.cpp streaming unaligned raw auto-powers \(S_{11}(f) = |X_1(f)|^2\) and \(S_{22}(f) = |X_2(f)|^2\) concurrently.
  • Network Channels: Dual independent UDP sockets to isolate kernel socket buffers:
  • Port 9998: SDR Channel 1 Auto-Power (\(S_{11}\))
  • Port 9999: SDR Channel 2 Auto-Power (\(S_{22}\))
  • Display Layout (4-Plot Symmetric Split-View):
  • Left Column (SDR 1 / \(S_{11}\)):
    • Top: 1D Auto-Power Spectrum \(|S_{11}|\) (\(10 - 95\text{ dB}\), yellow curve #ffdc32).
    • Bottom: 2D Rolling Waterfall (300 slots) with dedicated interactive ColorBarItem.
  • Right Column (SDR 2 / \(S_{22}\)):
    • Top: 1D Auto-Power Spectrum \(|S_{22}|\) (\(10 - 95\text{ dB}\), light cyan curve #38bdf8).
    • Bottom: 2D Rolling Waterfall (300 slots) with dedicated interactive ColorBarItem.
  • Status Bar: Real-time channel delivery metrics (complete, frame_gaps, late, invalid) and instantaneous gain balance \(\Delta\text{Peak} = P_{11} - P_{22}\) in dB.

docs.title: Mode 3: Advanced Hybrid & Multi-Scale Waterfall (viewer/viewer_fx.py)
docs.text:
• Primary Target: Advanced astronomical research combining fast transient detection with deep sensitivity integration and complex visibility phase tracking.
  • Backend Pipeline: Full FX Correlator backend outputting cross-power, optional auto-power overlays, and interferometric phase / coherence.
  • Network Channels: Configurable multi-port reception (1 to 4 UDP ports):
  • Primary Port (--port-s12, default 9999): Cross-power spectrum \(|S_{12}|\)
  • Auxiliary Port 1 (--port-s11, optional): SDR 1 auto-power \(S_{11}\)
  • Auxiliary Port 2 (--port-s22, optional): SDR 2 auto-power \(S_{22}\)
  • Auxiliary Port 3 (--port-aux, optional): Visibility Phase \(\Delta\phi\) or Coherence \(\gamma_{12}\)
  • Display Layout (Up to 4 Plot Widgets / 6 Data Streams):
  • Row 0, Col 0 (1D Multi-Curve Overlay Spectrum):
    • Fast \(|S_{12}|\) (\(200\text{ ms}\), yellow curve #ffdc32) for rapid transient monitoring.
    • Deep Integrated \(\langle |S_{12}| \rangle\) (\(N\)-frame linear average, orange curve #f97316) for noise-suppressed spectral baseline verification.
    • Optional background overlays of \(S_{11}\) (cyan #38bdf8) and \(S_{22}\) (red #f87171).
  • Row 0, Col 1 (1D Auxiliary Diagnostic - Enabled via --port-aux):
    • Interferometric Visibility Phase \(\Delta\phi \in [-\pi, +\pi]\text{ rad}\) (purple curve #a78bfa), or
    • Complex Degree of Coherence \(\gamma_{12} \in [0.0, 1.0]\) (emerald curve #34d399).
  • Row 1, Col 0 (Fast 2D Waterfall):
    • Single-frame resolution (\(200\text{ ms/slot}\), 300 history slots) for detecting micro-bursts and rapid frequency drift rates.
  • Row 2, Col 0 (Deep Integrated 2D Waterfall):
    • Multi-frame linear power integration (default: 5 frames \(\approx 1.0\text{ s/slot}\), 300 history slots). Provides \(\approx +3.5\text{ dB}\) additional noise floor suppression to extract faint, long-duration solar events (Type II/IV shock waves).

docs.title: Prerequisites on Host Workstation
docs.text:
Ensure your Python environment contains the required dependencies: 

pip install numpy PyQt5 pyqtgraph
Windows Firewall Configuration (run in elevated PowerShell if packets are dropped): 
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Solar UDP" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 9996-9999 -Protocol UDP -Action Allow

docs.title: Command Set 1: Running Mode 1 (viewer.py)
docs.text:
Listen on the default UDP port (9999) across all network interfaces: 

python viewer/viewer.py
Specify a custom bind address or port: 
python viewer/viewer.py --bind 0.0.0.0 --port 9999
Filter incoming datagrams to accept only packets from the Raspberry Pi 5 IP: 
python viewer/viewer.py --port 9999 --source-ip 192.168.1.15

docs.title: Command Set 2: Running Mode 2 (viewer_dual.py)
docs.text:
Run the dual-channel receiver using the audited default ports (9998 for Ch1, 9999 for Ch2): 

python viewer/viewer_dual.py
Explicitly customize UDP ports and bind address: 
python viewer/viewer_dual.py --bind 0.0.0.0 --port1 9998 --port2 9999
Lock to a specific transmitter IP: 
python viewer/viewer_dual.py --port1 9998 --port2 9999 --source-ip 192.168.1.15

docs.title: A. Standard Dual-Scale Waterfall (Single Port 9999)
docs.text:
Runs the fast \(200\text{ ms}\) waterfall and the deep \(1.0\text{ s}\) integrated waterfall simultaneously: 

python viewer/viewer_fx.py --port 9999

docs.title: B. Deep Integration Depth Adjustment
docs.text:
Set deep integration to 10 frames (\(2.0\text{ s}\) per slot, \(+5.0\text{ dB}\) noise floor suppression): 

python viewer/viewer_fx.py --port 9999 --deep-frames 10

docs.title: C. Cross-Power Overlay with Auto-Power Spectrograms (\(S_{11}\) & \(S_{22}\))
docs.text:
Overlay both receiver auto-power curves on top of the cross-power spectrum: 

python viewer/viewer_fx.py --port-s12 9999 --port-s11 9998 --port-s22 9997

docs.title: D. Full Hybrid Scientific Mode with Phase Tracking
docs.text:
Enables cross-power, dual auto-powers, and the 1D Interferometric Phase plot (\(\Delta\phi\)): 

python viewer/viewer_fx.py --port-s12 9999 --port-s11 9998 --port-s22 9997 --port-aux 9996 --aux-mode phase

docs.title: E. Full Hybrid Scientific Mode with Coherence Tracking
docs.text:
Enables cross-power, dual auto-powers, and the Degree of Coherence plot (\(\gamma_{12}\)): 

python viewer/viewer_fx.py --port-s12 9999 --port-s11 9998 --port-s22 9997 --port-aux 9996 --aux-mode coherence

docs.title: 4. Summary Matrix of Visualization Scripts
docs.text: Feature / Metric viewer/viewer.py viewer/viewer_dual.py viewer/viewer_fx.py Operational Role Standard Science Run Hardware QA & RF Calibration Advanced Hybrid Multi-Scale UDP Ports Used 1 (9999) 2 (9998, 9999) 1 to 4 (9996–9999) Total Plot Widgets 2 4 (2x2 Split) 3 to 4 **Cross-Power $ S_{12} $** Yes (Fast 200 ms) Auto-Powers (\(S_{11}, S_{22}\)) No Yes (Isolated Channels) Yes (Overlay Mode) Interferometric Phase \(\Delta\phi\) No No Yes (via --port-aux mode) Coherence \(\gamma_{12}\) No No Yes (via --port-aux mode) Dual-Scale Waterfalls No (Single 200 ms) No (Dual 200 ms) Yes (\(200\text{ ms}\) & \(1.0\text{ s}\) Deep) Zero-Roll Ring Buffering Yes (axisOrder='row-major') Yes (axisOrder='row-major') Yes (axisOrder='row-major') Timestamp Formatting Vietnam Time (UTC+7) Vietnam Time (UTC+7) Vietnam Time (UTC+7)

docs.title: 5. Backend Companion Execution (Raspberry Pi 5)
docs.text:
To stream real-time data to these GUI viewers, execute the corresponding backend target on the Raspberry Pi 5:

  1. For viewer.py or viewer_fx.py (Live Observation): 
    cd ~/solar_correlator
cmake --build build -j4
./build/solar_correlator
  2. For viewer_dual.py (Hardware Diagnostic & Calibration): 
    cd ~/solar_correlator
